lines.x: Our mission is to wipe out the sand bandits due to pass the target site, and to recover the shipment of medical supplies they seized — supplies that were bound for a nearby city.

Intelligence puts them at around fifteen, half of them discharged soldiers, so their equipment and training aren't poor. The leader especially is very cunning, and has slipped official pursuit many times.
Still, A6 has been running for a good while now.
The old us might have found this awkward, but I believe that for us as we are now, an enemy of this caliber isn't a problem we can't solve.
Mm!
Now let me assign the combat tasks.
Spot, same as always — you draw the enemy's attention.
Spot?
Hm? ...Mm. Give me a shout when it's time. I'll get back to my manga.
Did you actually hear a word I said?
Go out front and get hit, right?
Whatever. I only do what I'm able to do.
Let's finish quickly and go home. The new manga I ordered last month should have arrived.
I'm genuinely curious, Spot — why do you have so much manga to get through?
Because there's that much manga to get through.
Though the new stuff lately really isn't up to much. Neither the subject matter nor the writing does anything for me, so mostly I'm rereading the old ones.

Haah—
Midnight.
I know. My job is to engage them head-on with Spot and draw their leader out, right?
Oh, and here's the personal information I gathered on this bandit crew. You should all look it over — it'll definitely help with the tactics.
Wow, preferred weapons, dominant hands... Midnight, you're amazing, getting all this!
This one's got bad kidneys? This one has an eye condition?
Where exactly did you dig all this up?
These sand bandits love the village bars and pleasure houses. If you want information on them, that's obviously the place to go.
Just gathering information, were you? Why do I smell something odd?
It's the sunscreen the ladies gave me. Works wonders in the desert.
That's his story, Orchid. Do with it what you will.
...Enough. He messaged me about it partway through.
Spot, that trick of yours doesn't land anymore.
I wouldn't be so sure.
We'll settle up after the mission.
Uh-oh.
Popukar.
Orchid, I'm here!
Popukar, as A6's striker, remember: your task is to take down their leader.
You stay at the target site, and you don't move until Spot and Midnight bring the leader to you. Understood?
Yes, Orchid, understood!
I promise I won't budge an inch!
Popukar, haven't I told you? You need to learn to ask questions. You can't just believe whatever I say — you need your own judgment.
But everything you say seems fine to me, Orchid.

...All right.
You three head out first. Catapult and I will support you from the flank.
Mm!
Let's go, Spot.
Hang on, I've got sand in my shoe—
Haah. They say time grinds a team into shape. So why is it that after all these years, the oddballs on my team have only gotten more set in their ways?
Oh come on, Orchid, we've meshed pretty well, haven't we?
You're the last person I want hearing that from — problem child number one.
Where did you go just now?
I went to see whether there was anything worth hunting nearby.
Why have you taken such a liking to hunting these past two years?
I worked as a hunter for a while after leaving Kazimierz. I'm just picking up an old trade!
Which is why you skipped the briefing?
You give the orders anyway, Orchid. It's not as if you don't know me.
...Haah.
Oh, Orchid, A6 has been finding its footing for a long time now. It's been bumpy over the years, but here we are.
Sitting everyone down for a proper meeting at this point isn't realistic.
You're awfully relaxed about it. What worries me is that one day—
As long as that day doesn't come, it's fine, isn't it?
All right, Orchid, stop worrying. It'll be fine!
Orchid, this is the spot, right?
Mm. From here we can watch their movements and hold the high ground — the best position for ranged support.
True, the view's great.
Now we just wait for Midnight's signal.
Don't slack off. We need to watch the situation too.
Ye-es—
Say, Orchid, what are your plans after the mission?
No plans. Get back as fast as possible. HR still has plenty they need help with.
That's way too dull.
Out with it. What do you want to do?
It's not often we come all the way to Sargon. I want to look around nearby — an expedition, that is. An expedition!
What is there to explore in a desert? It's all sand, and the sun's vicious. Even the sunscreen I carefully picked out doesn't hold up.
Orchid, you're missing the point. We're already quite close to the foehn hotlands, and the foehn hotlands are one of every explorer's goals.
Columbia has apparently made some progress exploring them lately. They say the closer you get to the foehn hotlands, the more likely strange things are to happen...
If you want to go, take leave and go by yourself.
Huh? Can't we go together?
You're always saying we're a team, aren't you? A team should act like one. It's been ages since we did anything together.

...I'll think about it.
Hm?
What is it?
This is bad.
There are signs of a sandstorm approaching from over there, and it's closing fast!
What? Midnight and the others must already be engaged!
We have to warn them—
Midnight, be advised: a sandstorm is closing in. Don't get drawn into the fight. Pull back first!

Orchid...
It's bad...
We...
Popukar...
What about Popukar?! Midnight, answer me!
Catapult, something's wrong. Get ready to move in and support them!
Understood!
Orchid, the sandstorm's here!
Stay close to me. Keep track of each other!
(Shouting) What's happening?!
(Shouting) Ugh, I've got sand in my mouth!
(Shouting) The sand's too thick, I can't see. All I saw was a flash of light—
(Shouting) It looked like it came from Midnight's direction!
(Shouting) Quick, we have to find them!
...Where is this?
Weren't we in the desert just now...? Where's the sandstorm?
Wait, Catapult. Catapult?!
Orchid! Am I imagining it, or has the sand just stopped?
Orchid?
Ow!
Huh?
Orchid, where are we?
I was about to ask you.
We were in the sandstorm just now... right?
And then we walked and walked through it, and ended up here... This looks like... a bamboo grove?
I scouted that area. There was no bamboo grove.

Sargon doesn't seem the sort of place to have one.
This might be some kind of illusion...
No — where are the other three?!
Right, we have to find them fast!
But how? We don't even know where we are...

The comms terminal...
No good. No signal at all, and positioning is completely dead.
What do we do, what do we do—
Stop shouting. The more you shout the more anxious I get... Let me think—
(Higashi?) Stand down!
Orchid, did you hear that?
That voice... that's Popukar!
But why does it sound like she's speaking... Higashi?
We'll know if we go and look!
Tch — wait for me!
(Higashi?) Something has weighed on my heart these past days. The Wheel has already told me: the monster and the monster hunters must have descended. I must confirm that they exist.
(Higashi?) You ought to inform the Shogun of this.
(Higashi?) Moreover, if the monster has truly descended, the road ahead will be perilous indeed.
(Higashi?) You are the sovereign of Mirage. You bring down the will of heaven and point the way for us. The nation needs you.
(Higashi?) Since my mother vanished, he has borne every burden. What need has this nation of me?
(Higashi?) Your Majesty must not belittle yourself so...
(Higashi?) You prattle on. You truly have learned that man's tiresomeness down to the last detail.
(Higashi?) Stand down!
(Higashi?) I must find the monster hunters, whatever it takes.
(Higashi?) You must not!
(Higashi?) The Shogun has commanded it. If Your Majesty insists on forcing your way through, we will stop you even at the cost of our lives—
Popukar, you're... all right?
Er, when did you change clothes? It suits you, actually.
And who are these people? They don't look like the sand bandits we were after.
Popukar...?
(Higashi?) Who are you, and how do you know that my name is Baowuga?
Orchid was right after all. Listen closely and it really is Higashi. I'm forgetting everything Midnight taught me...
You've already forgotten it.

I have not! I'm still waiting to go sightseeing in Higashi one day. Don't believe me? Listen!
(Higashi) Ahem.
Popukar, where on earth did you run off to? We've been searching everywhere for you!
I have been here all along—
See? Told you I could do it!
No, I don't think it's that simple...
Popukar, don't you recognize us?

Why should I recognize you...
Wait. Your attire, and the tongue you just spoke... Could it be...
This is — the curse!
The "curse"?
Your Majesty, leave this to us—
What foolishness.
What reason have I to abandon you and leave alone?
Besides, I have already found the monster hunters I sought.
Then these two are—
There can be no mistake.
Orchid, is something off here...? Is this really the Popukar we know?
I'd say nothing about it is right...
Two travelers... will you help me hunt these cursed beasts?
...Popukar, what on earth—
If my guess is right, the two of you must be full of confusion.
When the hunt is done, I shall resolve your doubts.
What do we do, Orchid?
What else? Get ready to fight.
Ha, now that I'm good at!
Orchid, what's wrong?
Something's wrong with my umbrella—
Huh?
Then leave it to me! Take this!
Orchid, something's odd!
Why are these gloompincers so hard to put down?
That black miasma...
Popukar, what is this "curse" you were talking about?!
The curse is the calamity the monster brings. It fastens itself to beasts and makes them savage beyond measure.
The more I hear the less I follow!
Put simply, it's something that makes beasts more violent...
Is there no way to deal with it?
Once a beast is cursed, there is nothing for it but to destroy the beast with all your strength.
Otherwise, once the curse spreads, it brings about phenomena beyond all comprehension!
There's such a thing?!
No good. At this rate there'll be no end to it!
These cursed beasts must be destroyed here. Otherwise the curse will spread, and what's more—
Catapult, stop conserving ammunition!
Understood!
What now?!
Ow, ow, ow, my ribs...
Spot?! What are you doing?
Spot? Who's Spot? I'm Banmira!
Ban... mira?
I'm improving this kite.
Why is the kite so huge?
It's a man-carrying kite. Given a strong enough wind, this kite can lift you into the air.
And with a kite like this, surveying the surrounding terrain becomes far easier.
Ban... mira, since when did you get so fond of inventing things?
No, this is no time for that! We have to deal with these gloompincers!
Leave it to me!
Spot, you...
I knew it. He's all excuses on an ordinary day, but when it counts he's still the one you can rely on!
Wait—

Come on, Popukar, let's leave this to him—
What is it?
...Master Banmira is a smith of some renown in this land, but—
The man called Banmira stood on the slope, one knee to the ground, facing the approaching swarm of gloompincers. There wasn't a trace of fear on his face — what was there, remarkably, was excitement.
He set down the bundle on his back, drew out a long tube-shaped launcher made of bamboo, stuffed several brown spheres into it, and hoisted it onto his shoulder.

Whoa, that must be some kind of launcher!
Orchid, Spot's got skills after all!
...Something isn't right.
All right, let me try out this weapon I just developed! Its name is—
the shoulder-mounted bomb launcher!
And it's loaded with super-bombs of my own improved design!
Monster or whatever beast you are, every last one of you gets out of this area!!!
Ha! Spot, you may have changed your outfit, but I have to say, today you look incredible!
Huh?
The scene Catapult expected — the launcher on Spot's shoulder firing off some enormous bomb and driving back the gloompincers — did not occur.
Instead, the launcher on his shoulder exploded, the ordnance loaded inside it went up with it, and then—
a stench no one could bear began spreading rapidly outward with him at its center.
What is that smell?! It's revolting!
Oh no, I loaded the wrong ones. These are stinkbombs!
It stinks, it stinks!
What's a stinkbomb?!
Ugh— They are meant to drive beasts away with that pungent smell. But never have I smelled a stench so thick and so sickening—
That Spot — not only has he failed to drive the beasts off, he's going to see us off with them!
I put my faith in the wrong man!
(Feeble cries)
Yet the beasts dare not approach because of that smell. Now is our chance to break them one by one!
Ngh— urgh—
We're about to be broken one by one ourselves!
Samurai, Master Banmira — take the two monster hunters and fall back. I shall handle this!
Ngh...
Wait—
Orchid, what do we do? They've all pulled back.
Follow Popukar — no, Baowuga!
Hah, hah... Fighting while choking on that stench is no job for a person.
I'm plucking out a few tufts of Spot's fur later just to feel better...
Orchid, you've been frowning this whole time. What is it?
That Spot calls himself Banmira, and Popukar says her name is Baowuga. And they don't seem to know us.
And their personalities seem to have changed too. A self-possessed Popukar, a cheerful, funny Spot... Good grief, don't tell me there's a diligent, responsible Midnight as well.
You two need not follow me. I can handle these beasts alone.
As if we'd leave you on your own.
I—
Never mind that. I have a question for you.
Popukar — no, Baowuga. I really don't want to ask this, but—
Among the people you know, is there a man who's fairly handsome but has a dreadful personality and chases skirts all day long?
There is no such person among those around me.
Then do you know anyone by the name of Midnight?
Orchid, it wouldn't be that much of a coincidence.
I do.
...Huh?
The Shogun of Mirage is named Midnight. The people call him General Midnight of Mirage.
Loath him though I do, I cannot deny that he is a most serious and rigorous man who thinks of this country.
You said it yourself — a Popukar with her own mind, an unreliable but cheerful Spot...
And now a diligent, responsible Midnight on top of it... All right, I can't accept that either.
...Right? That's Midnight we're talking about!
The Midnight who, if everyone on this earth died but him, would mean the virtue of diligence had gone extinct!
I have a portrait of him here. You may see for yourselves whether he is the Midnight you know.
So saying, Baowuga drew a scroll painting from her robes and unrolled it before Orchid and Catapult.
There were three figures in it. A young Baowuga stood timidly beside an older woman whose brow and eyes bore some resemblance to hers — presumably her mother.
And beside the two of them stood a young man in samurai dress.
As a fashion designer, Orchid knew that adjusting someone's hair and clothing could give them an entirely different air.
Sometimes she had even thought that Midnight, properly tidied up, could pass for a clean-cut, good-looking man.
Though she had no desire whatsoever to test the idea herself.
And now she realized her thinking had been correct.
For the young man in the portrait had bright eyes and sword-straight brows, upright and commanding — every inch the pillar of a nation.
And that face was identical to Midnight's.
She couldn't help putting a hand to her forehead and sighing.
What on earth is going on—?!!!!
Orchid's scream circled through the bamboo grove and startled a flock of fowlbeasts into the air.

eps.name: The Coward Beneath the Hard Shell

lines.st: This land is a nation called Mirage, and we have lived by the hunt for generations.
What disturbs the peace of this land is the monster that descends from the Wheel roughly once every ten years, and the curse the monster brings.
This is the trial the Wheel has set for us.
The sovereigns of Mirage down the ages — my forebears — have borne, as priestesses of the Wheel, the duty of dispelling the curse and hunting the monster.

lines.x: Those beasts wreathed in black miasma just now — are those the monster?
No, those were merely beasts under the influence of the curse. Beasts touched by it turn exceedingly savage.
The monster is a beast of tremendous power, far beyond anything a cursed beast can compare to.
But if cursed beasts are left alone, the curse may spread, and that too becomes a thorny problem.
But you said earlier that we were the ones you were looking for. What does any of this have to do with us?
Every ten years, what descends from the Wheel is not only the monster and the curse. Two monster hunters come as well.
The monster hunters of every generation undergo the trial together with the sovereign, hunt the monster, lift the curse, and bring this land a brief peace.
Er, meaning... the two of us?
Yes.
Isn't there some mistake? Neither of us is any kind of monster hunter...
There is no mistake.
We of the sovereign's line share a strange bond with the Wheel. In recent days I felt it stir, and so I went out to search.
And your clothing, and the tongue you spoke when we first met, are nothing I know... The two of you must be the monster hunters the Wheel has sent.
Why must you people accept this so-called trial? It doesn't sound as though it does you any good at all.
It does. For us the trial is both a challenge and a gift.
Carry out heaven's decree; hunt the beasts of the earth. This is the maxim Mirage has kept for a thousand years.
...What became of the monster hunters of the past?
Once the hunt is complete, the sovereign absorbs the monster's curse and opens the Wheel anew. Most of them chose to return to their own homelands, though a few stayed.
Mirage's histories record the life of every generation's monster hunters.

Oh, so as long as we deal with this "monster," we can go home.
That's pretty convenient, Orchid.
Nothing is ever that simple...
Be at ease. I will not force you to accept all this at once.
The capital lies just ahead. Whatever questions you have can wait until we are inside.
Travelers from abroad, welcome to Mirage's capital — Mirage City.
Bamboo groves ring this land, and travelers often lose their way within them. Beyond the groves lies...
What is it, you two?
What is that...?
Which?
Er, that thing, in the distance.
Indeed — had it only been the sights within Mirage City, Orchid would not have been surprised.
But what stood before them now was strange enough that even Catapult noticed—
Far beyond Mirage City, a metal-sheened archway stood silently upon a snowy mountain.
Don't you find it odd? An enormous steel archway like that...
A steel archway? What a curious name for it.
That is the Wheel.
The Wheel...
Yes. The Wheel sent the monster here, but it also sent monster hunters such as yourselves.
Orchid lifted her head and gazed at the so-called Wheel.
Sunlight poured down onto the fine, cobweb-like carvings across the arch's surface, and in an instant hundreds of rainbow threads flashed back.
From afar it looked like a steel rainbow, majestic and holy. Yet for some reason, this beautiful rainbow left her deeply uneasy.
It is no wonder you are astonished.
The Wheel is our nation's treasure, a relic handed down by our ancestors from ten thousand years ago. It was not built in our time.
...I see.
If the Wheel interests you, I can tell you more about it later.
Aaah, there's too much I can't make sense of. I think my stomach's growling!
You don't need an excuse for being hungry.
...Let's go. There are so many mysteries already, one more won't hurt.
Look, it's Her Majesty Baowuga!
There are two people with Her Majesty! Could it be—
Huh, Orchid, look, the residents are gathering over here... People like us must be a rare sight.
Hi, everyone!
Haah... Never mind.
Your Majesty, are these two the monster hunters?
(Quietly) Baowuga... Your Majesty, there's much that isn't clear yet. Wouldn't it be better not to give them false hope for now?
Your Majesty, if the monster hunters have come, does that mean this decade's trial will proceed as usual?
(Quietly) Your Majesty?
...People of Mirage, as you see, these two are the monster hunters of this trial!
Thank goodness...
The gods preserve us. We haven't been abandoned...
People of Mirage, ten years ago the Lord of Thunder descended into the world.
At that time, Lord Masamune and Lord Yoshitsune, who had descended as monster hunters, went with the previous sovereign — my mother — to challenge the Lord of Thunder. However—
My mother failed to hunt the Lord of Thunder and vanished during the hunt, and Lord Masamune and Lord Yoshitsune were gravely wounded.
Such a thing was unheard of in Mirage's history. The histories had never recorded what would happen should a trial go unfinished...
At that time, the whole nation fell into confusion.
But today, everything has become clear—
The Wheel has not abandoned us! New monster hunters have come!
Are you truly the monster hunters?
We're...
Something like that.
You must be very strong, surely?
Heh heh, of course!
I give you my word: I shall carry on my mother's will and go with these two monster hunters to slay this cycle's monster and complete this trial.
And more than that—
To this day, the Lord of Thunder and the curse it brought still ravage the lands around Mirage.
Back then I was young. I could neither make you any promise nor avenge my mother. In my heart, the Lord of Thunder has been a thorn that cannot be pulled free.
I have held one wish all this time, and now I may speak it—
Once this cycle's hunt is complete, I shall go to hunt the Lord of Thunder... to finish the duty my mother left undone, and bring peace back to Mirage!
Wonderful... I knew Her Majesty Baowuga would find a way! Long live Her Majesty Baowuga!
Don't celebrate too soon. Don't forget what happened in the last sovereign's day—
Even so, Her Majesty is so young and already so dutiful. Isn't that something to be glad of? Long live Her Majesty Baowuga!
Tch, I'm not doubting Her Majesty!
...Long live Her Majesty Baowuga!
Wait, d-don't push me! My clothes! Don't throw me in the air!
Orchid, they're treating us like heroes!
But this isn't what she said earlier—
Ah, you're right. Ha ha. Who'd have thought we'd live to be taken in by Popukar.
Oh dear, and who was it who kept saying she wished Popukar would stand on her own two feet—
Be quiet!
I am sorry. I used you both.
Er, it's not that serious.
I rather like being treated as a hero.
But Orchid isn't like me — she can't stand this sort of thing. So if you're going to apologize, apologize properly to her.
Miss Orchid—
Ah, that teary-eyed look. It really is her.
Looks like you don't need to apologize after all.
Hm?
Orchid, you were just thinking "Popukar has finally grown up," weren't you?
Be quiet.
Haah...
There's a reason for it, isn't there?
...Yes.
The two of you are beyond doubt the monster hunters, and once the monster is destroyed you can return home through the Wheel. In that I have not deceived you in the slightest.
It is only that, in ordinary times, I as sovereign would never resort to such means — all but forcing this duty upon you.
This matter must begin with the previous generation...
The monster that descended ten years ago... was a nightmare hanging over the head of every soul in Mirage.
The monster now called the Lord of Thunder far surpassed all earlier monsters in strength and speed, and beyond that, it could command lightning at will.
It is just as I said in the square...
The previous sovereign, my mother, did not complete the hunt. Worse still, she vanished during it.
And that was unprecedented in our nation's history.
So long as the monster lives, the curse does not end.
For the past ten years we have had to face the Lord of Thunder's incursions at every moment, and the ever more frequent attacks of cursed beasts...
What frightened people more was this—
No one knew what to do. No one knew whether the Wheel would send down punishment, or whether something no one had foreseen would come to pass...
And as for me...
I have only one wish — to hunt the Lord of Thunder, avenge my mother, and bring peace to this nation.
Sounds like someone's stopping you. You're the sovereign — who would dare?
Midnight, is it?
...That is so.
After my mother's death, he governed in my stead while I was a child. In these ten years he has done a great deal.
He summoned all the hunters to the palace, declared that their standing was changed from hunter to samurai, registered each of them, formed them into hunting corps, and managed them himself.
It was from then that he took the title of Shogun.
The people have grown used to a life in which they cannot hunt freely, but at least we have survived beneath the Lord of Thunder's shadow.
I admit that without him the people's hearts could not have been steadied, and perhaps Mirage would not have lasted until today.
But faced with the very culprit that drove our nation to this state — the Lord of Thunder — he has never once thought to hunt it, and has even forbidden me from challenging it.
Why?
He always says the time has not come.
Then when does the time come?
...He demands that I complete at least three trials.
Three trials... thirty years?!
Because my mother had already been through three trials when she challenged the Lord of Thunder, he holds me to the same.
I cannot wait that long.
This is my first trial. In this trial I will prove to him that I have that strength!
...Which is why you rushed us into that position.
Yes.
Over these ten years, every time I meant to challenge the Lord of Thunder, he would appear behind me like a specter and counsel me against it.
I will not be looked down upon, nor will I let what was left unfinished ten years ago be put off any longer.
Your Majesty.
The Shogun's retainer? Go and tell the Shogun that I have found the monster hunters.
The Shogun already knows.
...Hmph.
According to the scouts, an unusually active swarm of Magma Snails has appeared in the bamboo groves east of the capital. It is highly likely they are under the monster's influence.
And the Shogun's meaning?
Since the new trial has begun as it should, he will not interfere with Your Majesty's actions.
From here on, I shall pass all relevant intelligence directly to you.
...Understood. Tell the Shogun I set out at once.
Yes.
Seems he guessed what you were thinking.
What a detestable man.
At least he doesn't appear to intend to stop you.
He is always thus. Watching me from afar, waiting quietly for me to admit to him that I cannot do it.
I will never concede defeat to him.
And so I ask you both to act alongside me. You need not join the hunt. I will deal with the monster and send you home.
I still have plenty of questions, but right now I only have one—
You said that in the past every monster hunt succeeded... Does that mean every monster hunter before us accepted this duty?
Not one of them ever thought of running, or refusing?
...That is not so.
In fact, the records say that at first, monster hunters who doubted and refused, as you do, were the majority.
Only, for one reason or another, they all came in the end to accept the duty and became monster hunters who hunted the monster.
The histories record it thus—

lines.st: The monster hunter is not chosen by the Wheel.
Rather, one knows one's own body, hears one's own desire, weighs one's own courage, takes up one's own weapon, and so takes up one's own fate.

eps.name: The Coward Beneath the Hard Shell

lines.x: Wait here, the two of you.
Just ahead is where the Magma Snail swarm appeared. This time, leave it to me.
...You really don't want our help?
If I cannot handle trouble even of this order, what right have I to challenge the Lord of Thunder?
Orchid, I'm honestly getting a bit lost.
Has the kind of thing that happens in Spot's manga actually happened to us?
...Don't jump to conclusions.
A trial once a decade, a monster, monster hunters, and that Wheel that fits none of it... It's all a bit contrived, don't you think?
And Popukar—
Orchid, are you saying this is all a hoax?
Remember we were in Sargon just now?
Certain Sargonian pashas get so bored they do unimaginable things on their own estates. This could be a vast film set built inside an oasis, for instance.

Whoa, I'd love to live like that too—
Er, no, by that logic I already am.
But then how do you explain those three?
A pasha's people often include all sorts of specialists. Perhaps their perceptions were altered.
Why them, though?
You're asking me? Who am I supposed to ask? I'm only raising a possibility.
If it is as I think, then at least the three of them are safe for now.
But if it isn't—
Hm?
Huh... Orchid, doesn't this thing look... a bit familiar to you?
...A large Originium Slug?
Ha! Orchid, now I believe you about this being a film set!
There's no such coincidence! Something is definitely wrong here!
It seems we need a strategy.
(A loud roar)
Looks like this fellow wants in on the strategy too, Orchid.
Haah.
Orchid, is your umbrella still not working?
I have no idea what's wrong with it!
Don't trade blows with it! Its movements are clumsy and it isn't bright!
Use the terrain — lure it into the bamboo over there!

Got it!
Hey! Big guy! Over here!
Now! Bring them down!
It worked! Look, Orchid! The bamboo's pinned it!
No — careful! It's breaking free! Look, the bamboo's catching fire where it touches that magma shell!
Wah! It looks even angrier! It's looking our way!
Scatter, quick! It's going to breathe fire!
We can't dodge it! The blast radius is too wide!
At that critical moment, a roar that shook heaven and earth came from not far off.
An immense blue-green beast strolled elegantly out of the woods.
The bamboo toppled like stacked blocks — as though bowing to a sovereign's arrival, or fleeing the approach of something demonic.
When the moonlight finally fell upon it, for an instant everything around seemed to freeze, even their heartbeats.
The horns on its head were like a crown, glinting coldly in the moonlight.

Its body was like a gem asleep in the dark of night, yet with every ripple of muscle it threw back a shattered white glare, as though thousands of bolts of lightning were caged beneath its scales, straining to break out.

As it strode forward, the earth shuddered first; every touch of claw to stone sent snaking arcs of electricity leaping up. A sweep of its long tail raised those arcs like a crescent moon tearing open the night.
The Magma Snail that had so troubled them a moment ago seemed almost endearing before it.
Wha... what is that? I've never seen a creature like it—
This thing... don't tell me that's the Lord of Thunder?!
It took out a large Originium Slug in a single blow...
Orchid, it's got its eye on us. Leave it to—
Don't get drawn in!
Hey, Lord of Thunder, try this!
(A low roar)
...Impossible. It doesn't have a scratch!
Waah!
Catapult!
Tch... If my Arts won't work, then at least—
Catapult, that was far too reckless!
Sorry, Orchid...
What you threw was a stinkbomb, wasn't it?
...I picked up a couple while we were running earlier. Popukar said they worked wonders for driving beasts off, so I kept it in mind.
That's our Orchid!
Still, so that's the Lord of Thunder... It's incredible.
Next time we see it, don't go swinging at it.
Okay...

You two! I thought I heard the Lord of Thunder's cry just now—
Did you—
Er, heh heh.
We traded blows with it briefly.
That was far too reckless, both of you!
Orchid already gave me a talking-to.
Thank goodness you are both unharmed...
I have cleared out every Magma Snail in this area.
Any sign of the monster?
...None.
Baowuga, are Magma Snails really creatures from around here?
Of course. Magma Snails have always lived in the lands around Mirage.
But going by the look of it, shouldn't it live somewhere like a volcano? This is a bamboo grove.
You may not know: beneath the Wheel lie snowy mountains, and beneath those mountains lies a region of magma.
That is where the Magma Snails dwell.
Your Majesty, may we begin clearing the field?
Go ahead. This area is safe now.
As expected of Her Majesty!
We thank the Wheel for its bounty and the priestess for her guidance. We, the people of Mirage, shall use these gifts of the gods with reverence.
Carry back all the Magma Snail carcasses, then harvest every usable material.
Yes, sir!
Er... what are they doing?
Magma Snails usually live in the magma region and rarely appear in numbers. Their shells can be made into firebamboo charcoal, which burns for a very long time.
Just so! This firebamboo charcoal is sturdy and useful, but Magma Snails are terribly rare. With this haul, we needn't worry about getting through the winter.
And why is that lot over there so cheerfully cutting bamboo...?
We make all manner of things from bamboo as it is. But a Magma Snail runs hotter than the largest furnace in this country, so it can bake bamboo until it's extraordinarily hard.
Bamboo baked by a Magma Snail we call blazebamboo.
Weapons or furniture made from blazebamboo are exceedingly durable.
Sounds fun — let me help!
...Is the trial the only way you can get this much?
It is.
The monster that appears in the trial once a decade, and the upheaval it stirs, have a great effect on the surrounding environment.
There is much danger in it, but it also brings us a great deal that we could never obtain otherwise.
And so for Mirage, the trial is a crisis and an opportunity alike.
Hunt the beasts of the earth, receive the gifts of heaven. This is Mirage's way.
Treating the effects of the trial as a blessing, and even depending on that blessing to live — that's far too unstable.
Oh? This blazebamboo is good stuff. It'd make nicely stable material for ordnance...
And has it truly never occurred to them to dig into the cause of all this?
Orchid, the Magma Snails must have come through here — the ground's covered in scorched flowers and grass. Some of them smell rather good.
Are you listening to me at all?!
I'm listening.
...I don't believe their account. We need to find a way to work out what this place really is.
Honestly, I think it hangs together pretty well.
Then you can stay.
Hey, it's not that I believe them. I just don't think their way of living is as impossible as you imagine.
In any case, that Originium Slug gave the game away completely.
If this really is a vast film set or a pasha's back garden as you say, we'd still have to take the three of them with us when we go, wouldn't we?
I know. From here, we split up.
I'll gather information. You're the better fighter, so you find out what happened to them.
Heh heh, now that I like!
Remember, the priority is investigation. Find leads, don't act rashly. Our ultimate goal is to rescue our teammates and get out of here together.
Understood!

Where should I start investigating...
Huh, over there—
Careful, don't knock it.
Er, what are you all doing?
Ah, it's the monster hunter.
We're carrying this Magma Snail carcass to the palace.
Weren't you going to make charcoal out of its shell? Why take it to the palace?

Purification? Can Popu— can Her Majesty Baowuga really do something like that?

There are things only Her Majesty can do.
So you're taking this carcass to her right now to be purified?
Can I come and watch how the purification works?
...I'm sorry. The place where Her Majesty performs the purification is sacred ground for rites. Even a monster hunter cannot simply enter.
If you truly wish to know, please obtain permission from the Shogun or from Her Majesty herself.
Stop standing about, keep moving. Her Majesty is waiting for us!
Tch. Your sovereign is busy preparing a purification, your Shogun is, er, somewhere I don't even know... That's just a fancy way of saying I'm not allowed to see it.
Hmph. If you won't let me see it, then I'll see it anyway.
I'm going to find out exactly what's going on in this place!
(If I assume my movements are being watched, then was everything I saw just now staged?)
(How can I find a crack in this place...)
(Huh, come to think of it, this doesn't seem to be a nomadic city?)

...If there's no nomadic city, how do you deal with Catastrophes?
Catastrophes? And what would those be?

Never heard of such a thing.
Has nobody here ever had Oripathy?
Oripathy?
The illness where stone grows on your body—
...Boom!

What's happened?

Master Banmira sets something off every day, doesn't he? Just leave him be.

(...Wait. Magma Snail shells — those are the Originium crystals on an Originium Slug's back! If those crystals exploded—)
(I'm such a fool. I should have realized the moment I saw those Magma Snail carcasses!)
(If it was an Originium explosion...)
(Tch — he'll die!)
Ow, ow, ow...
Spot!
I'm Banmira! Ow, ow...
Are you all right?!
I added some pressure to the gunlance. Didn't expect the thing to be so fragile.
I thought firebamboo charcoal would make nice solid ammunition, but it shattered the moment I fired and blew up everywhere...
Let me see!
Huh? What's there to see, it's just a scratch. I'm long used to it— ow, gently!

Just a scratch?! This is an Originium explo...
sion...?
Orchid looked carefully at the crystal fragments on the ground.

These... are ordinary crystals, not Originium...?
What's Originium?

Oripathy? And what's that?
Hey, what are you doing?!
Don't come near me, I'll call for help—
Somebody, help—
Orchid yanked up the front of Banmira's shirt.

Is there any kind of stone growing on your body?

Are you really not Spot?

What of it?

Beside the palace, that taller building.
I see.

(I have to find those carcasses.)
Thank you. Get some rest.
Hey, hey!

Let's see what she's actually doing...

What on earth is that "curse"?

And behind her, two neat rows of veiled attendants knelt.
All was silent.
Everything seemed holy and uncanny at once.
"Ring—"
"With this body as a vessel—"

That black miasma peeled away from the corpse as though drawn off by something.

Miss Catapult?!

That woman Orchid is truly baffling.
Haah, never mind.
Back to my research—
Huh?
(Tch, this thing's too quick. My launcher can't touch it!)

Hmph, don't get smug, little cloud beast!
Today I'm taking Popukar with me, no matter what!
I've no idea what you're thinking, meow. Interrupting Her Majesty's rite would only do her harm, meow!

Of course not, meow!
That's exactly why the monster must be destroyed, meow!
Excuses!
(Tch, no good. I'm nearly out of ammunition. I need something with more punch—)

What's happening?!
Ngh...

Tch, moving with this is even clumsier than I imagined!
A Charge Blade's weight is not the weight you go rolling about with, meow! And if you only defend—
Waah!
—you end up in danger like that, meow!

You're the enemy — why are you teaching me?!

Mind your own business.
(He keeps calling this pair a Charge Blade, but it's clearly a sword and shield...)
(Huh, there's a slot on the inside of the shield... axe... axe... I've got it!)
Hmph. In any case, it is time to end this farce, meow!
That remains to be seen!
Facing Masamune's charge, Catapult stopped defending and drove the sword into the shield's slot. The mechanism inside the shield engaged and the two fused swiftly into a single great axe.
Masamune's attack landed precisely at the instant the weapon changed form, but it failed utterly to interrupt Catapult's motion — and instead carried Masamune into her striking range—
Hah!
Ha ha! I see. Put this sword and shield together and they turn into an axe!
(She didn't even notice it herself — at the instant of transformation she blocked my attack, meow...)
(What a formidable one, meow.)

Watch this—
Ugh, it's heavy!
But you rely far too much on instinct, meow.
That will do.
Lord Masamune, stay your hand. She means no harm; there has merely been a misunderstanding.
Very well, if Her Majesty says so, meow.
Baowuga!
Miss Catapult, what I did just now was to purify the curse. It is the duty handed down through generations of priestesses. I do not need saving.
Duty, my foot! Look at yourself! You're just a child! You shouldn't have to bear this! You don't even know what you're doing!
I do know.
It seems there is someone near you whose name resembles mine and whose face is the same, and that has led you to misunderstand.
But I am not the Popukar you know.
That's impossible!
Then what proof do you have?

That's right — Popukar has Originium crystals on her arm!
Yours must have them too—
Baowuga said nothing, and merely drew back her sleeve. Catapult froze.
Baowuga's arm was white as jade, without a single mark.
(Hah... hah... I just hit it... but that one shot took almost everything I had.)
(No good. At this rate my own strength will run out before I bring it down.)
This is bad—
So the curse has grown severe enough to raise a beast from the dead... No, this is not resurrection. The curse is driving its body.
Someone.
Shogun.
Take this carcass away.
Should Her Majesty be informed of this?
...That won't be necessary.
Her Majesty need only focus on the trial at hand.
Yes, sir.
Miss Orchid.
You're... Midnight, aren't you.
I must thank you. Had you not bought us time, this Magma Snail would likely have caused no small number of casualties.
You're not going to ask why I'm here?
Her Majesty was too hasty after all.
She believed it enough to keep you settled, without considering that it would only lead you to misunderstand.
Part of my purpose in coming was to apologize to you on Her Majesty's behalf.
...I have a question.
Please ask.
Is your name really Midnight?
The genuine article.
(...I've never felt this before — how painful it is to hear such earnest words from that face.)
Her Majesty's rashness drew your suspicion, but you have also caused us some trouble. Let us call the matter even.
Catapult, is she—
She had something of a clash with the previous generation's monster hunter, but it has been resolved—
Orchid!
...Catapult.
It seems your companion has arrived.
Orchid, they... they really don't seem to be acting. Baowuga honestly seems to believe she has some kind of mission...

I know... There were none on Banmira either.
Catapult, this place may genuinely have no Originium. None of our common sense applies here.
Then... is this really not Terra, and those three really aren't the three we know?
Then we need to get back fast, Orchid!
...Baowuga told us the way back from the very beginning. We simply didn't believe her.

Regarding the trial, the hunt, and Her Majesty... I have a request to make of you, impertinent though it is.

This way, please.
I imagine you both have questions for me.
I don't, actually.
There are so many hunting weapons here. Can I play with them?
By all means.
Haah— Why don't you want Baowuga to hunt the Lord of Thunder?
And what do you think, Miss Orchid?
When I heard her say it, two guesses came to mind—

Catapult Style: One-Blade Cleave!
Hmph, as expected of Orchid — dodging a strike I've staked my life's work on—
Ow. That hurt.
Go and play over there.
Okay...
And the other?

And how do you see it now?
Now I think the two possibilities can coexist. They don't contradict each other.
Because you don't strike me as a man hungry for power, nor as a parent simply overprotecting a child.
May I take that as praise?
I'd rather you gave me an answer.
This is a flute, right? Let's see, where do I blow—
(Inhales)
(Plays)
Oops, did I disturb you?
Give it up, Catapult. You have no talent for it.
Tch.
It all... began with the previous sovereign's disappearance.

But the previous sovereign vanished in that last hunt, and every responsibility fell onto the shoulders of the young Baowuga.
What exactly... happened back then?
...I cannot tell you. Before the eyes of every one of us, she simply vanished.

Just so.

Huh, this gun is heavy. It's called a gunlance, I think? So can it fire shells...

Midnight, I've come to collect this cycle's monster hunters, meow!
There's a great deal more to tell them—
Meow?
Heave— ho.

Er, it seems this weapon doesn't suit me either... Ha ha... ha...
Meow...
CA—TA—PULT—!
Hah!

You're awake! Masamune! Thank goodness!

Midnight told us you'd bring us here.

This guy?

Whoa, this is the lowest-grade brawl I've seen in years...

Obviously!

I'm not going to— hm?

Done!

This...

—and you can move at high speed like that, meow.
Orchid, this bug is amazing! The silk held me and didn't snap at all!
The silk a Wirebug secretes is called ironsilk, and its toughness exceeds your imagination, meow. Movement is only the most basic use — it helps greatly in combat as well, meow.
Would Orchid like to try, meow?
Orchid, look, I climbed all the way up here with no effort at all!
Ha ha! This is so much fun!
Again— huh?
Meow meow! I hadn't finished — a Wirebug can't be used twice in a row! Someone has to catch her, meow—
You just said the ironsilk a Wirebug produces is very tough. Can it take the weight of two people?
Of course, meow!
Good.
Heh heh, Orchid really does look after me.
Stop clowning. The Wirebug is powerful, but it will take us a while to master, and there are various Silkbind techniques to learn. Don't waste time.
Ye-es!
It is such a relief that Orchid is dependable, meow...
Masamune, though — I have a question.
Meow?
You're the previous generation's monster hunter. If Midnight won't allow Her Majesty Baowuga to challenge the Lord of Thunder, there's no way he'd let you two roam freely instead.
And if you'd agreed with Midnight to wait until Her Majesty was ready before challenging it, you'd have no reason to bother with us.
Helping us would be meaningless, wouldn't it?
Don't misunderstand, I'm not suspicious of you. I simply don't much like accepting goodwill that has no reason behind it.
Orchid is a sharp one. To explain, I must start from where we came from, meow.
You mean you and your companion followed the Lord of Thunder here. So you and it once lived in the same place?!
That's right, meow.
"Lord of Thunder" is not its name, meow. It's only what the people of Mirage called it out of fear...
Its true name is Zinogre, meow.
Yoshitsune and I are members of Kamura Village's Hidden Team, meow. Our task was to go out and gather materials, and in doing so we ran into this Zinogre, meow.
While tracking it, somehow we ended up in Mirage, meow.
Then why did you stop me from interrupting Baowuga's rite? The Zinogre has nothing to do with this place, does it?
No — after coming here, the Zinogre did become connected to certain things in this place, meow. Interrupting Her Majesty's rite does no good at all, meow!
...All right.
That still doesn't explain why you'd help us.
You've already seen the curse, meow?
The cursed beasts give off black miasma and are far stronger than ordinary ones... Left alone, they'd do no less harm than the monster.
In my homeland — Kamura Village — there is something very like the curse, meow—
The Frenzy Virus, meow.
The Frenzy Virus...
It is a truly terrifying virus. Infected beasts give off black miasma all over and turn ferocious, meow.
The cursed beasts do have that trait.
You mean... you suspect that the curse spreading through Mirage, and perhaps the monster itself, came from your home?
Yes, meow... because the Frenzy Virus has a very definite source, meow.
But if that's true, then Mirage's trial would be—
I cannot say for certain, meow.
I can't guarantee the curse is the Frenzy Virus, but their natures do have things in common, meow.
All these years I have been searching for proof that the curse is the Frenzy Virus. If it truly is, then what I must do goes beyond what a monster hunter does, meow!
What are you doing, meow?!
Nothing. I just suddenly wanted to pet you.
Let's carry on training.
Shogun, the sun is nearly down. Might you take your leave?
It is Your Majesty who should note the late hour — it is past the time a child should be asleep.
How long does the Shogun intend to treat me as a child?
Until Your Majesty stops disputing the point.
You—
Miss Orchid!
What are you two doing standing here?
I am waiting for you and Miss Catapult.
I came to see whether you required any help.
Haah, I'm exhausted right now. I don't have the energy for you two.
Where's Banmira?
At your service, Lady Orchid!
Is the equipment finished?
It needs a little more time, but it will certainly be ready tomorrow.
Good.
As for you two—
Your Majesty, Catapult and I will accept the trial and go with you to slay this cycle's monster.
But whatever else is true, at present we have no guarantee whatsoever that we could successfully hunt the Lord of Thunder.
So if you want us to hunt it alongside you, forgive us — we refuse.
...I understand.
Thank you, Miss Orchid.
Don't celebrate too soon... I'm not agreeing with your view.
This is a judgment I made myself.
That is enough.
And as for now—
Dismissed.
Aren't you two going home yet?
The chance is rare. Perhaps I can be of some help.
I can help as well!
Hm?
Baowuga, hold still.
Hm?
There's a tear in your clothes. Come here, I'll stitch it up.
Hm? But...
It's no trouble. Come on.

Midnight meant to seize the chance to step forward and speak further with Her Majesty and the two monster hunters about the Lord of Thunder, but one glare from Orchid sent him retreating sheepishly back to the doorway.
Somehow he understood that look perfectly: "Now is not the time for that."
He was startled that he had read it, and more startled still that Orchid seemed to know what he was thinking.
The setting sun spilled into the old workshop, catching the dust drifting in the air and blurring everything.
The girl leaned obediently against the doorframe while the grown woman, a trace of worry on her face, silently stitched up the tear in her clothes.
And the young woman, under Masamune's instruction, joined and separated sword and shield again and again, as though the essence of the hunt lay within that motion.
For a moment, Midnight seemed to see a certain afternoon ten years ago.
The sunset had been just as lovely that day. He had stood guard outside the workshop keeping others away, and tiny Baowuga had toddled past him into it.
That day too, he had stood outside the door and glanced at what was happening within—
Banmira was studying his hunting gear as always, and the young Baowuga had happily picked up an axe and swung it about.
The previous sovereign had been discussing equipment with the master smiths, and seeing her daughter's movements, she paused the conversation and stepped over to guide her in how to swing a weapon.
Orchid bore not the slightest resemblance to the previous sovereign — she had been solemn and commanding, while Orchid was gentle and attentive. Nor did Catapult overlap with anyone in his memory.
And yet he could not stop himself from remembering that time.
Heh heh...
Why is Catapult smiling so happily, meow?
Orchid is finally back to her usual self.
Her usual self, meow?
Since we got here she's been frowning nonstop — well, she frowns all the time normally too, but it felt different.
What's the difference, meow?
Normally she looks like the world owes her a fortune. Since we arrived, she's looked like she owes the world one. Either way, it hurt to watch.
But she seems much better now. She's got her usual captain's air back.
Catapult cares a great deal about Orchid, meow.
Of course. She's our captain, after all.
Shogun, it's urgent!
What is it?
The snowy mountain... According to the scouts, something has changed on the mountain!
What?
The snowy mountain... has grown hot!

lines.st: Urgent Commission
Client: Baowuga, Sovereign of Mirage
Description
General Midnight's men report that something has changed on the snowy mountain, presumed to be the monster's doing.
The monster is Mirage's fated enemy. If it is not hunted soon and the curse spreads, the consequences will be beyond bearing...
Monster hunters, set out with me at once and complete this cycle's hunt!
Reward: The road home

lines.x: Monster hunter Catapult, ready to move out!
Have you got everything we need?
Let's see — tent, travel rations, fishing rod, telescope, pickaxe, bug net, barbecue set—
Reporting: all packed!
We're not going on an adventure holiday!
And where did you even get all that?
Kind folks in the city gave it all to me over the past two days. We are heroes, after all, and everyone's been so good to me.
Besides, these are all very useful hunting tools!
I fail to see how any of it helps with hunting a monster.
Familiarizing yourselves with the surroundings and terrain before the hunt is a legitimate approach.
What's the situation with the change?
The scouts report that while walking on the mountain, one feels waves of heat from time to time...
This is without question the monster's work.
Still, there is no need to rush. For now the change does not appear to have spread beyond the mountain.
We should deal with it sooner rather than later.
And by the look of her, Baowuga can't hold back any longer!
...I am holding back perfectly well.
The axe in your hand and the look in your eye say otherwise, Baowuga.
Something I'm curious about, though — does a hunt really need this many people?
I thought it would just be me, Orchid and Baowuga.
Of course, meow. This is no simple hunt, so the more the better, meow!
With me as your guide, you'll get twice the result for half the effort, meow!
And this fellow too, meow!
What a magnificent fanged beast!
(A threatening growl)
Ha ha, don't be so fierce!
Is he—
He doesn't quite trust you two, meow!
We will be moving with you, meow.
And the Shogun? The Shogun does not intend to come along with us, I trust?
Rest easy, Your Majesty. Of course I trust you.
Of late the scouts have found many signs in the bamboo groves of cursed beasts killing one another.
That is unusual, so I intend to lead a party and gather intelligence myself.
I merely came to see Your Majesty off along the way.
Rest assured. So long as the target of Your Majesty's hunt does not change, I will not interfere with it in any way.
Right now I would rather change the target of my hunt to you...
That too would be acceptable.
...Hmph.
Then, Your Majesty, may your hunt go well.
What about you, Banmira? Are you coming with us?
I can't be bothered.
If I didn't have to deliver your equipment, I wouldn't even have left the house.
Hurry and change into them. I didn't sleep a wink forging these two sets for you — I'm exhausted.
I'm going home to catch up on sleep.
Hee hee, new gear, new gear!
Haah...
Whoa, Orchid, this outfit really does fit perfectly.
Obviously. I altered the designs myself. If it didn't fit, the fault would be Banmira's craftsmanship.
Then his craftsmanship isn't bad at all.
I suppose not.
How does it feel in the new equipment, meow?
Mm... My body feels a little lighter, and my strength seems to have gone up too.
It does... The sensation is subtle, but I really can feel the strength... What principle is this working on?
It is a special forging technique, meow!
In any case, it's good for the hunt, meow!
Which means you don't actually understand it either.
(An agreeing growl)
Not so, meow! I am a member of the Hidden Team, not an apprentice at the Smithy, meow! Of course I don't know, meow!
Ooh, so this is my new weapon!
That's right. It's nothing like the one you grabbed on the fly, meow! This is a weapon that exists truly for the hunt, meow!
Heh heh... I really want to cut something right now.
Yoshitsune, I choose you!
(A disdainful growl)
Orchid, try shooting the apple off my head, meow!
Ha ha, Orchid says she isn't interested in hunting, and yet look how enthusiastic she is.
If I'm going to use this bow, then I'm going to use it properly.
You're the one who should be careful not to lose interest in three days as usual and start demanding a different weapon.
I won't!
I have a feeling the Charge Blade is the weapon I was destined for!
It had better be.
After briefly getting used to their gear, the two did not linger, and set out on the road with Baowuga.
Catapult's heart was full of anticipation for what lay ahead; she was thoroughly taken with her new weapon and genuinely hoped to face a stronger opponent.
Orchid, as ever, was full of worry. She knew the battle waiting ahead of them would be anything but easy.
Still, the new equipment she had adjusted herself suited her tastes perfectly in appearance, and that cheered her a little.
Ah, there is one more thing to do, meow!
What's that?
From here on, we may face battle at any moment, meow.
And if we are to fight, we cannot go without a hunter's feast, meow!
What, a feast?!
That's right, meow!
I shall treat you to Kamura Village's specialty—
What, will there be really good meat?!
Bunny Dango, meow!
Huh— When you say a hunter's feast, shouldn't it be mouthfuls of meat and tankards of drink?
Sweets... I'll pass.
That is prejudice, meow!
Once you've eaten the dango, you will know your error, meow!
Bunny Dango really isn't bad. I feel all warm inside and full of strength!
Naturally, meow! Bunny Dango doesn't only fill your belly — different flavors grant hunters all sorts of marvelous effects, meow!
I have... a bad feeling about this. The air here is deeply unpleasant.
It is the scent of the curse, and it grows thicker.
Huh? Don't you all feel... that it's not so cold anymore?
It isn't your imagination. Look at your feet!
They looked down to see the thick snow under their feet melting at a visible rate, exposing black volcanic rock beneath.
The air around them turned quickly hot and dry, and even began to fill with the smell of sulfur.
What's going on, meow?! How does a snowy mountain become a volcano, meow?!
It is the monster's curse... It is using its own power to reshape this place into a battlefield better suited to itself!
On the distant snowy peak a column of fire shot skyward, and then boiling magma poured down from the summit, staining the white snowfield a startling red.
Waaah! It really erupted!
I can feel an immense power gathering within the mountain... It must be the Magma Snail. It means to use the curse's power to turn this entire mountain into a volcano!
No, that isn't right... The curse's energy is not in one place alone...
There are two separate points, and the one within the mountain is by far the greatest!
What did you say?!
It must be stopped!
Suddenly the ground beneath them split into a vast fissure, and scalding magma surged up from it, cutting the party apart in an instant.
Miss Orchid! Miss Catapult!
Orchid! Baowuga is—
Tch, so that's its game...
Wirebug— damn it, this magma is in the way. The Wirebug can't get across either!
Mm... Then it must be this way.
You two, I shall deal with the energy within the mountain. Just find a way to keep yourselves safe!
Baowuga, wait!
Tch, why does that child insist on taking everything on alone!
Orchid!
Well then, perfect timing, meow.
Let us see the fruits of your training, meow. Yoshitsune, we fall back, meow.
Yoshitsune let out a low growl, as though saying "don't disappoint us."
Huh? You're not joining in?
This is your first test, the examination that decides whether you are fit to be called hunters, meow!
Catapult, ready?
Heh heh, of course!
I'll pin down its movement with Arc Shot — you find an opening and hit its legs!
Got it! Watch me close in with Morph Slash!
Oh? Orchid's judgment is very accurate, meow. Break the hind legs first and it will go down, meow.
Yoshitsune gave a short, sharp cry, as though pointing something out.
Hm? Yoshitsune asks why you keep opening the distance, Orchid, meow. Your arrows are accurate, but you seem to instinctively avoid the danger of close quarters, meow.
(So I've been seen through...)
Orchid! It's about to use that fire breath! Now's the moment!
Catapult, dodge! You can't take that head-on! It's far too powerful!
No! I want to try! The manual says the strongest Charge Blade is the one that meets the strongest attack!
You fool! Don't do anything rash, meow!
(This idiot — she's actually going to take a magma blast head-on, meow!)

Waah! So hot! I did it...
But... my body's all numb...
You're hurt! Fall back!
Not a chance! Watch me finish it with this!
What is she doing, meow?! The Magma Snail is about to counterattack! Does she mean to take it down with her, meow?!
Catapult!
Super Amped Element Discharge!
Heh heh, Orchid, did you see that?!
You—
Uh-oh... my body feels so light—
Haah. Idiot.
The campfire crackled to one side, driving back the cold.
Orchid crouched on the ground, carefully tending the wounds on Catapult's body, her brow furrowed.
Heh heh. Orchid, I was so cool back there! The Magma Snail was tough, but—
Orchid's hands pressed a little harder.
Ow, ow, ow, Orchid, gently.
Haah. I knew it. Put that weapon in your hands and this was always the likely outcome.
Ye— sss, that hurts! But Orchid, don't you think it's fun? Hunting is wonderful.
Looking at the state of you, I fail to see the fun.
It's that feeling of... giving it everything, and beating an opponent countless times stronger than you with wits and courage!
I have no wish to understand it.
All I see is that for the sake of looking "cool," you stopped listening to my orders.
I wasn't disobeying orders! I...
Yoshitsune was right.
Huh? What did Yoshitsune say again?
That I instinctively avoid close-quarters fighting. He was right.
But what about you, Catapult? Masamune said you went too far as well. Don't you think you were gambling with your own life back there?
(Masamune said I went too far too... but if I don't do it that way, it feels like... like I'll miss that one instant...)
(That feeling of your heart about to burst out, of staking everything on a single moment...)
I really don't understand what hunting means to you.
Catapult tilted her head at that. She wanted to answer with a quip as she always did, but for some reason the words stopped at her lips.
Silence settled between them, with only the sizzle of the grill to show that time was passing.
I see. So this cycle's monster was a Magma Snail of such size.
First you enslaved an ordinary Magma Snail, meaning to use the curse to turn this whole mountain into a volcano — a place better suited to your kind.
Then you scattered us, intending to break us one by one.
But you made two mistakes...
First, you failed to realize how strong Miss Orchid and Miss Catapult are.
Yes — you must feel it yourself. The curse has weakened greatly. That lesser source of it is already gone.
They have destroyed your underling.
And your second mistake was making an enemy of me.
Now die.
(A feeble roar)
Ngh—
What is happening?!
Baowuga felt something beneath her feet, deeper and farther below the earth, drawing her in.
The pull was so strong that she felt her very soul being drawn out of her body.
Immense pain filled her, until even breathing was difficult.
At the same moment, the fallen Magma Snail's corpse erupted with black miasma that surged skyward, and as the miasma thickened, it slowly dragged itself up from the ground.
Its shell split open, revealing what lay beneath — a substance with no shape to speak of, its nature beyond description, nothing more than a torn piece of space.
And yet it existed there, solidly, upon the monster's back.
Gah—
Its attacks are several times fiercer than before...
(An enraged roar)
It has turned the surroundings entirely into a volcano...
What is it trying to do...
Does it mean to trigger an eruption?!
I will not let it succeed!
Ngh...
Why — what is wrong with my body—
Leave it to me!
Catapult?!
Catapult, stay focused!
I know!
Miss Orchid, you two—
Heh heh, looks like we got here in time!
Baowuga, what's happened to you?
I... do not know. Only that I can feel some unspeakably vile power drawing at my body...
Don't worry, leave this to your big sister Catapult!
This thing must be the real monster. Beat it and we can go home, right?
Orchid, cover me!
Super Amped Element Discharge. From the first time she heard the name, Catapult had thought it magnificent. She liked it a great deal.
What she liked more was the intent of it: strike the ground with the axe, ride that force, let the Wirebug carry you high into the air, and swing!
First check the element phials' charge. No problem, fully charged. The red light on the shield flashed as though urging her on.
Watch the prey — the Magma Snail had left an opening after that last guard. A perfect chance.
Leap — strike the ground with the Charge Blade for the initial momentum, and at the same time let the Wirebug haul you into the air. Ha, whoever invented this was a genius!
It's not going to get back up again, is it?!
Rest easy. The monster is truly dead.
Baowuga, you...
My body is fine now. I can feel that whatever was pulling at me has gone.
What exactly was it?
I... do not know.
Still, you may both rest easy. We have completed the hunt. Now I shall follow tradition and send you home.
Congratulations, Your Majesty.
Spare me the pleasantries, Midnight.
I am sincerely glad for Your Majesty's victory and for the monster hunters'.
If you are glad for us, then you should let me go after the Lord of Thunder.
That is a separate matter.
Enough — listening to you two gives me a headache. The monster is dealt with, so what's the next step for getting home?
Next, Your Majesty purifies the monster's corpse, activates the Wheel, and sends the two monster hunters back.
And the Homecoming Festival?
Your Majesty.
It is tradition.
A festival?
The festival is both to give thanks for the Wheel's bounty and to bid farewell to the monster hunters.
We carry the monster's corpse back, and I purify it through the rite.
Then the people take the most useful parts and craft them into weapons or tools, which are given to the monster hunters as keepsakes.
The rest becomes food or decoration, and part of the festival.
And at the festival's close, I activate the Wheel and send the monster hunters home.
Midnight, would you have the two monster hunters believe our nation knows nothing of gratitude?
...In times past, hearing that the monster had been hunted, the people of Mirage might well have rejoiced.
But now the Lord of Thunder's influence has not lifted. This is no time for a festival.
Even so—
Stop.
What do you think, Miss Orchid?
We were in a hurry to get home to begin with. Even if you did hold a festival, I'm not sure I'd be in the mood.
The people of Mirage have already shown us more than enough kindness. You don't need to do anything further.
Besides, Midnight is right. In an emergency you adapt. Let's leave it at that.
Thank you for understanding, Miss Orchid.
But is this really all right with you?
...Yes. This is enough.
What did Orchid mean by that question to Her Majesty just now, meow?
She was asking Baowuga whether hunting the monster Magma Snail really was enough.
And Baowuga answered that it was.
How strange, meow. Isn't Orchid the one most eager to go home, meow? Why did that question sound as though, if Baowuga wanted to dig into the Zinogre, she would help, meow?
Isn't that asking for trouble, meow?
That's just how Orchid is.
She says she doesn't want to meddle in other people's trouble and only wants to do her own job, and then before she knows it she's involved herself anyway.
And then she dresses it up as: "What else was I supposed to do?"
That sounds awfully contradictory, meow.
Orchid is a very contradictory person, meow.
Don't copy the way I talk, meow!
Saying bad things about me behind my back again?
Not at all. I was saying you're the best captain in the world.
I'll believe that when the sky falls.
Miss Orchid, Miss Catapult — since we must adapt to circumstances, I shall perform the rite here.
Fine.
Please stand back.
What is she going to do?
I know — Baowuga's going to dance again.
Watch, Orchid. This might be the last time we see it.
Dance?
That's right.
With this body as a vessel—
As she danced, the black miasma remaining on the Magma Snail's corpse began to be drawn off, slowly and in order, and absorbed into Baowuga.
Her face grew paler and paler, yet her gaze was extraordinarily steady.
The miasma passing through her body seemed to be "filtered" by some power, until it became pure, colorless energy that surged toward the Wheel behind her.
The Wheel's arc began to give off a soft white light, brighter and brighter, and then a silver-white door appeared at Baowuga's side.
It worked! Orchid, look! We can go home!
Catapult, wait! Something's wrong!
Huh—
Heed my command—
At the very instant the Wheel's light reached its peak, it went out without warning. Sound and color seemed drained from the world, leaving a deathly stillness.
The pure white door turned black in the blink of an eye, and then a far deeper darkness came pouring out of it.
This thing... it looks like a fanged beast, but it isn't one at all... What is going on?!
Curse-fiends... Why would curse-fiends appear here?!
Curse-fiends?!
Midnight, what is this?!
Curse-fiends are forbidden...
In Mirage's history there was once a great calamity, in which a pack of wolves tainted by the curse destroyed the Mirage of old.
Those curse-tainted wolves are the curse-fiends.
Our ancestors who survived that calamity rebuilt Mirage and then hunted the wolves in the surrounding lands to extinction...
Wolves... you mean fanged beasts?
Baowuga, curse-fiends keep pouring out of this door! Isn't there something we can do?!
I cannot!
Something is stopping it from closing!
These curse-fiends... their very presence foretells disaster. Have I summoned them—
Don't lose your head. This isn't your fault, Baowuga!
Exactly, Your Majesty. There was nothing wrong with what you did! Something else must be—
They looked up in terror to see, on a distant cliff, a colossal beast covered in blue-green scales and wreathed in blue-white lightning, its head raised in a roar.
It stood high on the cliff, looking down upon everything unfolding below.
The Lord of Thunder?!
Did that thing interfere with the Wheel?!
Lord of Thunder, was it you... Have you been waiting for this very moment all along?
Is the reason you never disrupted my hunt that you were waiting for the moment I activated the Wheel?!
Answer me!
Answer me—!!!!
Your Majesty, do not act rashly!
The Lord of Thunder is destroying the trial!
Would you stop me even now, Midnight?!
I—
Suddenly a loud, urgent bell rang out from the foot of the distant mountain.
What's that sound?!
That's an alarm, meow!
It's the hunting corps' emergency alarm... It isn't sounded in ordinary times, unless—
Shogun, terrible news!
Vast numbers of curse-tainted beasts are pouring from the foot of the mountain toward the Wheel and out of the bamboo groves.
They are closing on the capital!
Pass the order: the hunting corps is to form a line at once. Whatever happens, the beasts must not reach the capital!
And you, Shogun? We need your command!
I— I will return to the capital immediately.
Yes, sir!
Not only has that thing blocked our way home, it's summoned a horde through the door... But why would it—
No time to worry about that. If you want the thieves, take the chief first!
The Lord of Thunder is the leader of these beasts, isn't it? Baowuga, let's cut our way to it right now and finish it!
Baowuga?
Catapult stepped in front of Baowuga and tugged at her, only to find she wouldn't move an inch.
Only then did she see Baowuga's expression—
teeth clenched, and utterly helpless.
Catapult, don't talk nonsense.
How can you guarantee that Mirage won't be destroyed by the curse-fiends before you ever reach it?
But those black things pouring out of the door are endless!
Dealing with it now is the best chance, isn't it? Who knows where it'll run off to next!
Don't forget — only Baowuga can dispel the curse.
—Aaargh, damn it! Why does it have to be this complicated! That rotten Lord of Thunder!
At the very least, until we find a proper method, we can't gamble with Mirage's safety.
But—
The Lord of Thunder is right there! Miss this chance and who knows when the next will come!
In the past I stopped Her Majesty from hunting the Lord of Thunder because, in the end, it had not yet bared its fangs at us.
Now that the Lord of Thunder has become the source of this disaster, however, I can hardly stop Her Majesty from wishing to strike it down.
However...
There is no need to say it.
Miss Orchid is right.
I am the sovereign of a nation. Even if I cut my way to it now, what meaning would any of it have if Mirage were destroyed before that?
Back to the city. Prepare to meet the beast tide.
A wise decision, Your Majesty.
Baowuga turned and walked toward the capital.
Before she turned, she looked long at the Lord of Thunder on the distant peak.
As though to carve the sight of it into her soul.
Shogun, Your Majesty, you're back at last!
How stands the situation?
Reporting to Your Majesty! Beasts are still pouring in without end from the direction of the Wheel! They... they simply cannot be killed off!
The defenses the Shogun has built over the years are holding, but it is likely only a matter of time before they break.
...Well done. Pass the order: have them hold a while longer. The line must not collapse. Her Majesty and I will find a way.
Yes, sir! We believe in you and Her Majesty!
Such grand promises. And if you cannot keep them?
Morale matters most to any force. Confidence outweighs everything.
Easy to say. Pure defense only buys time with lives. It is a slow death.
The Lord of Thunder is now the leader of this beast tide. Miss Catapult was right: provided the capital's safety is assured, killing it first remains the best choice.
I understand your meaning, Your Majesty.
But the tide comes on fiercely. We must resolve what is in front of us first.
I shall lead the troops myself and destroy the tide. We are the people of a hunting nation. If we die, we should die in the hunt.
You must not.
Your Majesty might kill ten beasts, or a hundred, but by the scouts' observation the tide has no end.
Then what plan have you?
...First, let me state a pessimistic conclusion. With Mirage's present strength, holding the tide head-on is almost certainly impossible.
Give me another thirty years to prepare and perhaps I could raise a force able to withstand it.
I know. As we are now, we cannot meet it head-on.
Just so. We must strike out and split the tide.
Split it how? By your own account our forces are already stretched thin. Doing that is no different from cutting our fragile line in two.
I understand your concern, Miss Orchid. Which is why this operation is not a frontal assault but a stratagem. We have... a one-of-a-kind bait.
Bait?
The monster Magma Snail we just slew. Its corpse.
You'd use its corpse?
Just so. You have both seen the curse, Miss Orchid.
It is an ill-omened energy, and beasts eaten away by it are instinctively drawn to a stronger source of it — as moths to a flame.
But didn't Baowuga already absorb its curse?
I absorbed only the energy needed to activate the Wheel... The curse upon it was not wholly dispelled.
And to beasts tainted by the curse, that corpse is a feast they cannot resist.
Using a hunting target to lure hunting targets — very much a hunter's style, meow.
But where will we lure them, meow? On open plains we cannot outrun an endless tide, meow.
Midnight's finger came down on a long, narrow stretch of the map: the bamboo groves beyond the capital.
Several miles east of the city, beneath the surface of this bamboo grove, lies a vast hollow — the remains of an ancient underground river that dried up long ago.
You mean to—
Just so. We send an elite unit as bait, use the monster Magma Snail's corpse to draw the bulk of the tide into this grove, and then—
Use Banmira's custom explosives to blast the surface, cause a large-scale collapse, and let them fall to their deaths.
The plan sounds workable, but... why is it that I knew nothing of a hollow here?
This place...
Wait, meow. Isn't this where the previous sovereign—
...Just so. That hollow is the Lord of Thunder's lair.
That is precisely why Your Majesty has searched the whole region for years without finding its lair.
I had no wish to tell Your Majesty of this place, but in an emergency one adapts.
I shall go myself.
I hunted the monster Magma Snail. The curse upon it resonates with my priestess's power, so the lure will work best if I drag the corpse.
Forgive me... I cannot obey that order, Your Majesty.
Midnight! I am the sovereign of this nation and one of Mirage's strongest hunters!
Even now, do you still fear I will rush off to challenge the Lord of Thunder on impulse?
For ten years, whatever the Lord of Thunder was doing in the shadows, it did not bring us utter ruin.
That gave us time in peace.
Even if that peace was a humiliating one, so long as it was peace, I would defend it to the death. Call me a coward or a reactionary for it; I do not care.
But there is one thing I would have you believe: everything I have done in these years has been to lay the road for you to kill the Lord of Thunder.
It is only that we still do not know how the Lord of Thunder caused this upheaval.
It is not yet time.
I have heard that far too many times. When exactly is the right time?
Why must you always arrange everything for me?
...Because I have seen things Your Majesty has not.
Your Majesty remaining in the capital is the greatest encouragement to the people's hearts and to morale.
Mirage as it is now needs you.
You are always like this.
Miss Orchid, please remain in the capital and assist Her Majesty.
I intended to anyway.
But are you certain the strata at that spot will blow open? If it fails, the bait unit will be swallowed whole by the tide.
I trust Banmira.
I can help too!
...Catapult is our strongest individual fighter right now. Midnight, take her and Yoshitsune. Run the rest as you planned.
Understood!
(A roar full of fighting spirit)
Masamune, you stay with me and help Her Majesty hold the city.
No problem, meow! I will keep a close watch on Her Majesty, meow!
Midnight.
Your servant is here.
...Come back alive.
I will.
Er, Your Majesty, I know you're in a foul mood.
But could you please not take practice swings inside my house?
I cannot bear to stay in the palace.
And being in my house improves your mood?!
You are on decent terms with Midnight. Swinging where you can see me lets off a little steam.
I wouldn't call our terms decent.
I've been wondering about that too. Why is the great General Midnight on good terms with you of all people?
And why are you here in my house as if it were nothing? Is my house an amusement park?!
I can't bear to be in the palace either, and this is the only other place I know.
Tch.
Ten years ago I was still an apprentice, and he was only the previous sovereign's shadow.
My master joined her expedition and was killed by a cursed beast, and the previous sovereign vanished afterward.
Since then he's come to see me now and then, calling it shared misfortune, if you please. Hmph. I don't feel any shared anything.
Don't you hate the Lord of Thunder?
Of course I do. That's why I've kept researching new equipment — waiting for the day someone kills it with a weapon I made.
...So you were serious all along?
I never once said I wasn't serious. People simply didn't believe me.
And only Midnight has kept encouraging me. But that's all it is. He helps me and I can't help him, so it hardly counts as friendship.
That isn't how friendship is counted.
Come on, Baowuga. Staying here won't help either.
Let's go and see whether anything out there needs doing.
Cold wind passed through the bamboo leaves with a sobbing sound, like the murmuring of ghosts.
An elite unit of thirty hauled the mountain-like corpse of the monster Magma Snail through the trees with specially made ropes and rollers, making slow progress.
Black curse miasma crawled slowly across the corpse like something alive, giving off a sweet, rank smell of sulfur and rotting flesh. Any bamboo it touched blackened at once.
So this black miasma really can affect the environment. How strange.
What is the curse, Midnight?
Many have studied the curse, but no one has ever reached a firm conclusion.
All we know is that if a person stays near the curse too long, or eats the flesh of a cursed beast, they too fall under its influence and die strangely.
And if a place is steeped in the curse too long, it becomes deeply uncanny and difficult to approach.
East of Mirage there is a bamboo grove where, a century ago, the curse upon a monster erupted. To this day that grove remains forbidden ground.
...It's a wonder you've survived in a place like this.
Nature tests us greatly, but it gives us much as well. That is fair enough.
