Ha, I like that. Better than fretting about respecting the animals, respecting the plants, oh dear, hunting is so barbaric.
Do you mean Miss Orchid?
I never said that. You did.
And you? Do you enjoy hunting, Miss Catapult?
Me? I... don't know.
Shogun! A great many beasts have surrounded us!
Just as planned!
Don't look back! Don't get drawn in! Keep your speed — the target is two miles ahead!
Midnight, you all press on. Leave this to me.
Are you sure?
I don't know whether I like hunting, but I definitely like this new weapon!
Don't get in my way!
...Understood.
Try this!
Tch, this thing's tough!
Don't run—
Yoshitsune?!
(An impatient growl)
Fine, your temperament's a lot like mine — don't go stealing all the glory yourself!
How about a contest to see who takes down more?
(A disdainful growl)
Hah, if this were a volcano I might be panicking, but I've learned my lesson already!
Catapult swiftly shifted the Charge Blade back into sword-and-shield form, and the gloompincer locked against her lost its opposing force and lunged into empty air.
In the instant another gloompincer's fangs were about to reach her, the shield in Catapult's hand met them at an exquisite angle. It was not a simple block but a kind of welcome.
The impact cracked the earth beneath her feet, yet she did not budge. She felt clearly how the enemy's force was converting into her own energy through the shield.
My turn!
How's that, Yoshitsune? Not bad with a Charge Blade, am I?
(A grudgingly approving roar)
Ha ha, you really are proud.
All right, enough chatter. Let's go and find Midnight together!
(A rousing roar)
This is the place! Cut the ropes, everyone fall back to the designated point! Hurry!
The samurai cut the ropes, set down the corpse, and spurred their mounts toward a rise at the edge of the clearing.
The beasts lost all reason. Their eyes held nothing but that enormous corpse and its enticing scent.
They swarmed forward, packing the entire clearing, biting and trampling one another for the best position.
Good grief, so many... If this had reached the city...
Banmira, I hope you prove reliable this time.
Did you fire the signal flare?
I did.
Er... did it fail? Why is there no reaction at all?
Impossible. The calculations...
It worked... The detonation went smoothly.
The ground... the ground is splitting! With that corpse at the center, the whole surface is dropping!
They fell! Every last beast fell through!
Ha ha ha, what a sight!
Don't celebrate too soon, Miss Catapult. Count the casualties, and then—
Shogun! Beneath us! This rise we're standing on is splitting too!
You're joking?! This is going to collapse as well?!
This is bad! The collapse has exceeded the projected range! Pull back, now!
A huge boulder rolled past them and scattered the formation.

In the confusion Catapult and Yoshitsune were shoved aside by the rock, while Midnight, saving several samurai who nearly fell, was cut off by another wave of collapsing earth and lost contact with the main force.
You need not follow me, nor worry for me. I gave Midnight my word, and I shall keep it.
I believe you.
I'm just... a little worried about you.
...There is no need. This trial is my trial.
You were sent here by the Wheel. Mirage was already in your debt.
Now the monster is hunted, yet the Wheel has failed and you cannot go home. I can scarcely face you.
All of this is a responsibility I must bear.
You're holding yourself far too tightly, Baowuga.
The trouble with the Wheel clearly isn't your doing either. Neither Mirage nor you owes us anything.
Thank you for your kindness, Miss Orchid.
But whatever else is true, getting home must be the most important thing to you, isn't it?
...It is.
I will certainly find a way to send you back.
I'm not trying to hurry you. It's only—
Is it because there is a child at your side who looks just like me?
How did you—
From the way you treated me when we first met, and the name "Popukar," I had my guesses.
You must care a great deal for that child. That is why you care so much about me.
...That isn't the reason.
Perhaps it was at first, but it isn't now.
Then why?
Caring about others is simply what one does.
But I do not need it. I have said as much. I can solve these problems alone. I am capable of it.
You are like Midnight — deep down you believe I cannot, don't you?
...If anyone else said that, I'd assume they were putting on a brave face. But I know you're capable of it.
Then why—
In a way, I understand Midnight's thinking.
Perhaps he isn't afraid that you can't do it. Perhaps he's afraid that you can.
In the capital, everyone was shaken by the enormous noise and the towering dust from the distant bamboo grove.
It worked! General Midnight did it! The tide in the east... is gone!
He does have his moments.
He is always like this... taking every danger onto himself.
By the sound of it, the two of you should be the closest of allies. How did it become this — always at odds?

My mother was busy with affairs of state... It was he who was always beside me. He taught me to fight and read with me. When my mother vanished and I had only just taken the throne, it was he who shouldered the most troublesome duties in my place.
I am grateful to him. But I cannot bear the look in his eyes whenever the Lord of Thunder is mentioned.
He has never truly restricted my actions, yet his gaze seems to say: "Go ahead and try. When you fail, you will understand."
...Midnight does have his own faults. Here's an idea: when he's back, let's all have a meal together.
And talk properly about the Lord of Thunder. How's that?
...Very well.
Where's Midnight? Where is he?!
The Shogun saved us, and... and the collapse carried him to the other side!
Suddenly she heard a familiar roar from afar, full of regal authority, and froze. The sound pierced the dust and the din and struck straight at her soul.
That sound... don't tell me — the Lord of Thunder?! Why is it here?! This is bad!
Yoshitsune, let's go!
(An anxious roar)
(Those are... Midnight's samurai? All of them down... and all these beast corpses around... What happened here?)
(Midnight?!)
(How is he... hurt this badly! His armor's in pieces... his blade snapped... Hey, you're joking, don't you dare die!)
Midnight! Hold on!
(This is bad! I can't move! This presence... where is it coming from?! The pressure is terrifying... my body won't obey at all...)
(My head... I can barely lift it...)
(An enraged roar)
(That's... the Lord of Thunder?!)
(It looks... strange...)
(That black mist... that's the curse, isn't it? Rising from those beast corpses...)
(Wait, the Lord of Thunder is glowing? What is that? White light...)
(This light... I've seen it! Exactly like when Baowuga danced! How is that possible?!)
(It's... it's absorbing that black miasma! With Baowuga's power?!)
(Why?! Why would a beast use the sacred power handed down through Baowuga's family?! Unless...)
Having absorbed all the curse, the Lord of Thunder seemed satisfied.
It lowered its head, glanced with cold beast's eyes at Midnight on the ground, and then threw back its head in a deafening roar.
That roar seemed filled with endless majesty and... a declaration of victory.
When Yoshitsune brought Baowuga, Orchid and Masamune to the scene, what they saw was Catapult kneeling beside Midnight, utterly stricken.
Mid... night?
Orchid, you're here!
He's not dead, but he's in a terrible state!
We heard the Lord of Thunder's roar and came straight here!
What on earth happened?!
I don't know either. By the time I got here, the Lord of Thunder was already—
The Lord of Thunder... Did it do this to Midnight?!

I... don't know.
But I saw it! It— it was using your power!
Exactly like when you purified the corpse at the palace! It drew all the black miasma from those beasts... into its own body!
What did you say?!
No... impossible...
Truly, meow?! You couldn't have mistaken it, meow?
(An affirming growl)
It... it not only killed my mother... it took the priestess's power that was hers...
So that is it. No wonder it could reverse the door I opened. No wonder it could summon curse-fiends...
So that is it. Heh, heh heh... So that is it.
She knelt beside Midnight, reached out, and gently wiped the blood from his face.
She did not cry. Not a single tear.
Baowuga...
Seeing their commander fallen and hearing such appalling news, the samurai around them lost all heart.
The Shogun is...
That monster... it can take even the previous sovereign's power... We're finished...
A monster?! Didn't you say there was only one monster per cycle?! Why is there another one?!
Tch — what a mess.
Masamune, Baowuga, we pin it from the flank and look for a weak point!
Baowuga?!
(An enraged roar)
Out of my way.
Catapult, we—
Do not come near! I can handle it alone.
Baowuga...
Good timing...
Baowuga—!!!
She is unharmed, meow!
She's insane! She used the blast itself as cover and propulsion just to close on the Magma Snail!
Is she... is she purifying the Magma Snail directly?!
Don't do anything foolish, meow! Your Majesty, this takes a terrible toll on your body, meow!
But Baowuga was deaf to everything around her.
She simply pinned the Magma Snail down, and however it thrashed, she did not move an inch.
Until its body slowly went limp.
Baowuga! We can help you!
...It is not enough.
Baowuga rose. Without looking at anyone she walked straight to the edge of the sinkhole, her bearing that of someone about to cast aside everything behind her and leap alone into the abyss.
Stop!
This is no longer your concern.
What about your soldiers? What about your nation? They're all watching you!
Baowuga slowly turned her head, and the hollowness in her eyes chilled Orchid.
Right now I... can see nothing. I want only its life.
Your Majesty, please... think again.
Midnight has fallen. Will you now stop me in his place?
It is precisely because the Shogun has fallen that I must say this in his place—
Hunting the Lord of Thunder must be planned over the long—
Baowuga, don't act on impulse!
The Lord of Thunder has already harmed my nation! It has harmed Midnight!
How would you have me stay calm?!
We followed the Shogun day and night. Now that he has fallen, our hearts grieve beyond measure.
And it is precisely for that reason that we keep his teaching: hunting the Lord of Thunder must be planned for the long term!
Whoa—
Move aside!
All of you, stop!
Miss Orchid, please—
He really has taught you lot to be as pigheaded as he is.
What matters most right now is getting your Shogun onto a stretcher and back to the city for treatment! He isn't dead yet!
Then leave a detachment here to stop any beasts climbing up out of the sinkhole!
But—
No buts!
Understood. Do as Miss Orchid says!
Yes, sir!
And then there's you, Baowuga.
I don't care what's going through your head right now. But if you're going down there, so am I. If that thing doesn't die, we can't go home.
I won't tell you to put aside your hatred; that would be hypocritical. But you know better than anyone how strong the Lord of Thunder is.
So we'll go and hunt it with you.
...Very well.
(From her eyes, she isn't convinced. But there's no other option right now...)
Miss Orchid...
I never promised your Shogun that I'd stop Baowuga from hunting the Lord of Thunder.
But—
Your Shogun must have told you what the hunting corps exists for.
So that Her Majesty may hunt the Lord of Thunder.
And isn't that exactly now?
You... are right.
(Quietly) This is the best option we have. I'll do what I can to steady her.
...We place everything in your hands.
Bring me paper and a brush.
Hm?
I'm writing a letter. Tell Banmira to give it to your Shogun when he wakes.
Understood.
Masamune, Catapult, Yoshitsune! Get rope and lighting ready!
We're... preparing to hunt.
It's no use! The gate is about to break! Use the rollers and the oil!
Their eyes! Their joints! Those are the weak points! All of you, on my command, concentrate fire on their weak spots!
(Gleeful howls)
The samurai on the walls loosed arrow after arrow, but it was like dropping stones into the sea. Nothing could meaningfully wound those thick-hided beasts.
No good... they're too tough...
Enraged by the harassment, the beasts drew back a few steps, let out a deafening roar, and hurled themselves at the gate with even greater force.
We're done for—!
I knew it. Without the Shogun and Her Majesty we can't hold!
...No. It isn't time to give up yet!
Her Majesty and the two monster hunters have already gone to hunt the Lord of Thunder. We must hold until then—
Hold until when?
...If only for the Shogun's sake, we must protect this capital!
The Shogun has protected this nation for ten years. Now it is our turn to protect him!
Run if you must. I won't blame you.
...Forgive me, Captain.
Run. It's fine to run.
Hmph. Beasts — your dying day has come.
Midnight still remembered the last time he saw the previous sovereign.
Your Majesty, please reconsider.
The scouts' reports are grim. This monster is far stronger than any in the records. We are not fully prepared, and the expedition... has already lost nearly half its number.
Will you still not listen to me?
Your body... do you think I haven't noticed? The blood you coughed up in the courtyard that night, the stark black stain on that handkerchief!
The curse has eaten deep into you already. To go and fight now is no different from taking your own life!
If you will not think of yourself, then think of the nation! Think of Her Highness Baowuga! She is so young — she cannot be without a mother! And Mirage cannot be without you!
Is it my fault? Am I not strong enough, that you must go into danger yourself again and again? Say the word — one word — and I will give you everything!
So please... I beg you... stay. Don't go.
Why... why do you go anyway?
Stop! I order you to stop!
...No... I have no right to order you...
I beg you... don't go...
That was the last time he saw her.
We have already lost the previous sovereign.
Mirage cannot lose Her Majesty Baowuga as well.
Her Majesty is gifted; given time she will surely grow into a sovereign as fine as her mother.
But time — yes, we need time...
For the sake of time, so that Her Majesty may grow up safely...
I would rather she hate me, and pour all her hatred for the Lord of Thunder onto me.
At least that way is safer.
And yet—
Is this right?
Hah... hah...
What a stubborn brute...
Heh... Shogun, it seems I'll be going on ahead of—
Captain!
You fool, why have you come back?!
I— I, I wasn't running away. I went for help!
Doesn't the Shogun always say that to stay alive, nothing is shameful?
You fool! Going for help only drags others down with us!
It's not like that!
You lot, get clear!
Is that... artillery fire?!
Banmira sat astride a thoroughly ridiculous-looking machine.
It was built entirely from bamboo, shaped like a vehicle, and left one genuinely wondering how it functioned at all.
Yet no one could underestimate it, for the smoke rising from its barrel proved that the powerful shot just now had been its work.
Master Banmira?!
This is the fruit of my own research, using Catapult's ranged weapon as the blueprint!
See that?! One shot wiped out this many cursed beasts!
I've named it Banmira's custom Dragonator!
There's such a wide space down here.
Ssss— this water is freezing!
But the water over here is hot! Why?
The terrain around Mirage is rather unusual, meow.
Beneath the snowy mountain lies a magma belt, where ordinary Magma Snails dwell. We have already passed through it, meow.
Baowuga, look, this moss glows!
Mm.
Catapult, could you please stop acting like a child on her first camping trip...

But it's interesting.
Right, Baowuga?
Mm.
Baowuga...
I am fine. Do not worry.
(Sniffing)
(A warning growl)
...Just as I thought, meow.
This was the camp we once used as a resting point. Hunting the Zinogre proved far harder than expected, and the previous sovereign mounted several expeditions, meow.
Each time, we used this camp. Finding it means our direction is correct, meow.
...Wait. This camp, it looks like—
Yes. This camp was not built by us. It has been here since far more ancient times, meow...
We merely borrowed it back then, meow.
What is it, Baowuga?
In Mirage's histories there is a passage—

lines.st: Of old, when the Wheel lost its measure, calamity touched the eight quarters, and sun and moon gave no light;
the remnant folk forsook the old soil, divined for new land, and so preserved their line to this day.

lines.x: Ahead is where the previous sovereign vanished, meow. It is far too dangerous there. Midnight originally meant to wait a few more years and gather enough strength before entering, meow.
Midnight...
Lord of Thunder, I will kill you...
Ah, my apologies, meow!
(Quietly) Orchid, what do we do? Baowuga looks like she won't hear a single word!
(Quietly) Us coming along doesn't help. Only Midnight can stop her!
(Quietly) I know.
(Quietly) What we have to do is keep her from doing anything stupid.
(Quietly) As for Midnight... I've made arrangements.

(Quietly) Arrangements?
Don't tell me... I saw you write something before we set out and hand it to a soldier.
Don't tell me...
That was a letter for him.
I've found him irritating for a long while.
Ngah...
Awake?
At least you're awake. Much longer and you'd have started turning into a monster by the look of you.
How do you feel?
The plan?
Relax. Your plan worked.
Most of the beasts fell into that great pit. Heh, my explosives are something, aren't they?
...Rather too much so.
Her Majesty, and the monster hunters — where are they now...
They saw the half-dead state of you and set out to hunt the Lord of Thunder.
What?!
Don't fret too much. Orchid and Catapult went, and Masamune and Yoshitsune too.
Speaking of which, that Orchid really is something.
She's always saying she hates taking on responsibility, yet when it mattered she was the first to step forward.
The soldiers who were there say Her Majesty was close to breaking after seeing the state of you, and Orchid stepped in and steadied the situation.
Her Majesty went to hunt the Lord of Thunder... because of me?
That's right. Because of you.
I labored ten years so that Her Majesty would not have to risk hunting it alone...
And in the end it was my own hand that set her on that road.
Is this the fate of the priestess?
I thought that on hearing Her Majesty had gone to hunt it, you'd leap up and rush to her side.
Weren't you afraid of her taking the risk?
...You don't understand, Banmira.
What I feared was never that Her Majesty could not do it.
What I feared was precisely that she could... and that even if it demanded a price, she would pay it without hesitation.
Just as the previous sovereign did — vanishing before our eyes without hesitation, and never returning.
I revered the previous sovereign more than anyone, so I know that in her heart there was you, and me, and every soul in this nation — and no room at all for herself.
And Her Majesty Baowuga inherited that sense of duty.
I wanted to share that burden for her. I wanted to give her a choice — so that when she meant to pay the price, someone could pay it in her stead.
And now... heh, ha ha...
...I didn't expect it to be exactly as Orchid said.
What?
She had a samurai tell me you'd certainly be despondent when you woke, and asked me to look in on you.
Otherwise I couldn't have been bothered to come.
...Hah.
She wrote a letter. Read it yourself.
...What?
When you wake and hear Baowuga set out with us, you'll surely decide all those years of effort meant nothing, and your heart will go cold.
If I've guessed right, then I have something to tell you—
Miss Orchid...
If you're going to play the good man, then play it to the end, you coward!
Miss Orchid?!
At first I thought you were different from him. Now I see you're exactly the same!
Obsessed with appearances, forever putting on a show for others. You say you want to bring everyone smiles, and the moment you can't take it you give up on your own and try to run.
Do you think Baowuga will thank you for what you've given? Do you think the previous sovereign, if she were alive, would cherish your sacrifice?
Don't make me laugh.
If in your heart the previous sovereign and Baowuga took everything upon themselves, then let me ask you—
how is your way any different from theirs?
Yes, you followed her for years, you watched Baowuga grow up, you know them better than anyone. And so what?
Are the previous sovereign and Baowuga unreasonable people in your eyes, and only you, Midnight, see the bigger picture?
But... neither Her Majesty Baowuga nor the previous sovereign was wrong. The sovereigns of Mirage, the priestesses of the Wheel, have always acted this way. I could not persuade them.
Was it that you couldn't persuade them, or that you didn't want to?
Were you truly thinking of them, or did your heart hold the same thing theirs did — that if only I make the sacrifice, everything will be all right?
I did not.
...No. I did think that.

I'm not trying to blame you.
All right, I am a little angry. But you should see it yourself: you weren't wrong. And you weren't right either.
Baowuga is the same. There is another way, and the two of you act as though that way doesn't exist and go off with your own.
Not only that, you each claim it's the other who doesn't want that way.
Whatever you two think, from where I stand as an outsider, that's how it is.
I won't ask you to do anything, Midnight. I only hope you'll calm down and think it through — what can you actually do for Baowuga?
Die for her? Fine. If that's the conclusion you reach after real thought, I won't stop you.
But surely there are other things you could do.
I—
...Banmira, could you give me a hand up?
Miss Orchid is right.
There was such a way all along, and because I did not trust Her Majesty I chose to bear everything alone.
Deep down I always treated her as a child in need of protection, arrogantly believing that only I saw the fragility behind her strength. But that was not so.
I was too concerned with my own feelings.
No — you're just like Her Majesty. You both disregard yourselves so thoroughly that others have no choice but to worry for you.
These ten years, the first lesson every hunter learned on joining the corps was that they exist so Her Majesty can hunt the Lord of Thunder.
That's a cruel thing, because they no longer hone their craft for themselves, nor hunt for themselves. I hate that, which is why I never once considered joining.
And yet in ten years, not one person has left the corps.
Because they can see that you, General Midnight, are the one hardest on himself. If the day ever comes when someone must give their life for Her Majesty's hunt, you'll be the first.
More and more samurai gathered behind Midnight. He knew them, of course — every one of them his own elite.
Give the order, Shogun.
The weapon Master Banmira developed helped us hold back the tide. Let us go to Her Majesty's side!
What can I... do for Her Majesty...
Back then... why...
Could it be... no, that can't be...
What is it?
...Banmira.
I must reach Her Majesty as quickly as possible... There is something I must tell her.
We must not press on rashly from here.
The Lord of Thunder's trail ends here. It seems this is where it dwells.
In this... bamboo grove? But why is there bamboo underground? Could this grove be connected to the one above?!
No. This grove is the Lord of Thunder's doing.
Do you see the drifting mist? That is the scent of the curse, though not the curse itself.
Others have witnessed such mist between the peaks, and no small number have lost their way within it.
This proves we are not far from it.
I'll go take a look.
Catapult!
Huh?!
Why are you coming from behind me—
You must not act rashly.
It is the Lord of Thunder's dwelling here that has made this place what it is.
It seems denser than ten years ago, meow...
(A slightly hesitant growl)
The Zinogre is a monster that favors dwelling by streams. By instinct it has made this place its lair, meow.
Ten years ago, the previous sovereign passed through this grove countless times, meow.
This grove is so uncanny that countless members of the expedition were lost in it and never returned, meow.

lines.st: That day, Her Majesty entered the grove with us once again, meow.
At one moment the mist abruptly cleared, the uncanny air coiling between the stalks was swept away, and a path suddenly appeared before us, meow.
I thought the Wheel had at last heard my prayers and was showing us the way, meow. But when I ran to the end of that path, all I saw was—
a bloodthirsty great beast, and a wisp of black smoke dispersing, meow.

lines.x: ...Huh?
What is it, Miss Catapult?
Baowuga, are you glowing?
Hm?
Indeed, Her Majesty's body is glowing, meow!
This is—
Baowuga drew a small vial from her robes.
Inside, a winged insect was beating against the glass, its tail faintly luminous.
This is...
That is a Thunderbug, meow!
A Thunderbug?
Thunderbugs are insects that live in symbiosis with the Zinogre, meow.
This is the last thing my mother left me.
All these years I have kept this insect with me. To me, seeing it was like having my mother still at my side.
But in all these years it has been quiet and has hardly ever glowed. So why—
It looks like it wants out. Why not let it go and see?
Baowuga nodded and opened the lid. The Thunderbug drifted lazily out of the vial, then flew slowly toward the depths of the grove—

The deep sea of bamboo seemed to wake quietly. Points of the same light rose one after another from the ground, from branches, from behind withered leaves — scattered like stars, flickering, like lanterns stirred by wind on a rainy night.
The grove's native shadow was washed thin by that faint glow. When the wind blew, the shadows of swaying leaves drifted gently across the ground, like paper cuttings adrift on blue-green ripples.
Baowuga stopped and raised her hand slightly. A Thunderbug brushed past her fingertips and spiraled upward, trailing a brighter flicker of lightning.
Motes of radiance scattered down from above, like a rain made of light.
The others stood beside her, holding their breath without meaning to — as though the slightest sound would scatter this quiet dream woven from blue light.
In that faintly glowing sea of bamboo, time seemed to have its pulse held by the green stalks, leaving only a soundless beating.
And over that beating, the Thunderbugs' dance laid a soft, unspeakable peace.
It's beautiful.
Ha, let me catch a few to take back!
What is it, Baowuga?
If they live in symbiosis with the Lord of Thunder, they too must come from that distant land... So why are they not at its side?
I do not know... This sight is beautiful, and yet I feel such sorrow.

Thunderbugs...
That's it — the Thunderbugs, meow!
Yoshitsune, you sensed it too, didn't you, meow!
(An approving growl)
What is it?
Orchid, look!
The Thunderbugs, which had seemed to fly at random, had gathered at some point into a long, slender band of light through the grove, leading deep into the mist.
Lord Masamune, is this the path you spoke of?
That's right, that's right, meow!
(An excited growl)
So it was never a path at all, but a passage lit by these Thunderbugs, meow.

lines.st: So... that is how it was.
Lord of Thunder... but for your strength, I could never have come... this far...!
A pity... that everything... is too late...

lines.x: What's that sound?!
That voice... it's as if the grove itself is speaking...
That is... my mother's voice?!
Mother! Are you here?!
Tell me — what happened?!
Why is your power in the Lord of Thunder? Did it kill you?
Baowuga, don't act rashly!
Baowuga!!!
Orchid, Baowuga's gone already!
After her!
We have to find her fast! If these words are the previous sovereign's last message left in some form... Baowuga won't be able to control herself!
This is — a waterfall?
The ground is covered in curse-fiend corpses, meow! Her Majesty killed all of these, meow!
(An agitated roar)
There she is!
The corpses of curse-fiends stretched on and on, and at the end of that road of bodies Baowuga stood at the waterfall's edge, staring blankly down.

lines.st: The Lord of Thunder... its power... is devouring me...
Baowuga, my beloved daughter... you must... become stronger than it... and take back... everything that was ours...

lines.x: These words...
Tch. For Baowuga as she is now, these words will only goad her!
These curse-fiends have impeccable timing!
Baowuga, wait for us—!
I have already seen where the Lord of Thunder is.
Wait, we'll go together—
Once I have killed it, I shall come back for you.
Then you may go home.
She— she just jumped down?!
Orchid, we'll have to cut our way through!
I know!

lines.st: No... do not repeat my mistake... Activating the Wheel... is the only hope... Use the Lord of Thunder's power... do not... be devoured by hatred...

lines.x: Wait, this passage...
Could it be—
Damn it. Could the truth be nothing like what we imagined?
Orchid, what did you say?!
I said we have to reach her as fast as we can! Otherwise it will all be too late!
At last... I have found you.
Lord of Thunder...
The Thunderbugs tried to draw near the Lord of Thunder, but before they could reach it the black miasma rising from its body flung them away.
(An anguished howl)
I see... So it was the curse that kept these Thunderbugs from you. No wonder they seemed so sorrowful.
Lord of Thunder, is living in this land that is not yours also a thing of great pain for you?
Let me end that pain.
We finally cut through—
Orchid, look over there, at the center of the ruins, on that altar! Baowuga is fighting the Lord of Thunder!
Haaah—!
You are strong indeed.
Then so be it—
The priestess's power erupted fully in that moment. Light wrapped her in an instant and spread swiftly, covering the Lord of Thunder as well.
Gah—
As I thought. It will not go so smoothly...
But I prepared myself long ago.
If I cannot take back my mother's power from you, then at the very least I can—
What's that light coming off her?! Is she using her power to absorb the curse from the Lord of Thunder?
No... that's wrong! Absorbing the curse doesn't look like that!
That is... she is using her own priestess's power to resonate with the previous sovereign's power within the Zinogre, meow!
Resonate...? Don't tell me—
She means to take the Lord of Thunder down with her?!
(An anxious roar)
This is bad, meow! Drawn by that power, the curse-fiends that fell into the sinkhole and the cursed beasts are all converging on the altar, meow!
At this rate Her Majesty will be swallowed by the tide, meow!
We have to find a way to stop the tide reaching Baowuga first.
But how?! We're far too far from that altar! Even a Wirebug wouldn't get us there in time!
Catapult, Masamune — ride Yoshitsune to the route the tide must take, directly below that altar, and buy me a little time!
Meow?! But—
No time to explain. Trust me!
Let's go, Yoshitsune, Masamune!
Haah...
Every last one of them, nothing but trouble.
This position... this angle... there should still be time.
The instant she saw this space, Orchid had already worked out the answer.
She raised her bow and aimed at the distant rock face, where a great mass of sharp stone spikes hung directly over the route the curse-fiends had to take.
Bringing those spikes down was hardly simple, but she had keenly noticed the instability of that stratum. She only had to strike it with enough force and enough precision.
She could do it.
Even she was a little surprised by that confidence — just as she had been surprised at herself for stepping forward to upbraid those samurai and Baowuga.
Would the old her have done it? ...Really?
She drew the bow and began to build the shot.
In that moment countless thoughts surged through her mind, yet the tangle of them did not confuse her. On the contrary, she felt her focus had never been sharper.

At first I thought the ones here in Mirage were better versions of them.
A self-possessed Popukar,
a cheerful Spot,
a rational, restrained Midnight.
But later I found I was wrong.
They have their own problems, and at heart they are almost identical to the ones we know.
If Popukar hadn't been brought to Rhodes Island by Dr. Kal'tsit, if Spot and Midnight hadn't joined because of Oripathy...
If they hadn't joined Squad A6... no, if we had never formed A6.
Perhaps their temperaments wouldn't match these three, but every one of them would have gone on living, stubbornly, by their own strength.
And in the moments they faced hardship, the only thing they could think to rely on would be themselves.
When a person has only one option, that isn't a choice.
But I always told myself I still had to respect them as they were.
So I would advise people without stopping them, and only help once they'd failed. I called that respect.
But—
What I wrote to Midnight, I was really writing to myself.
What can I actually do for the people I care about?
She released the string.
What's wrong with Orchid? She's been odd ever since we came underground, meow!
Orchid is... torn.
She always puts on that face of none-of-my-business, strictly-professional, but she cares deeply about the people around her.
She cares so much that she doesn't know how to show it, so in the end she chose that face to hide behind.
And in time she fooled even herself.
Of course she cares about our squad. But...
Since she stepped up and took charge back then, she'll think of something now as well.
Let me tell you a little secret, Masamune.
We never say it aloud, but whenever someone in A6 is in trouble, one line always surfaces in our minds—
Orchid will think of something.
With a whistling sound an arrow flew over the heads of the tide, like a meteor streaking through the dim underground ruins.
A Dragon Piercer, meow?!
The "meteor" struck high on the rock face, and then a violent tremor rolled through.
It's going to collapse, meow!
Ha ha! That's Orchid for you!
The tide is blocked! Orchid's calling us to Baowuga's side. Let's move!
Just a little... more.
She was matching her power against the Lord of Thunder's, neither side yielding.
But that little more... was a hair's breadth and a world away.
...As a priestess, as a sovereign, I prepared myself long ago.
To close that final gap, she need only pay with her life.
And to her, that had always been the most trifling price of all.
Mother, watch over me.
So long as it was for Mirage, for her mission, for her duty...
And even setting those aside — if only to send Miss Orchid and Miss Catapult home.
It would still be worth it.
I will... kill the Lord of Thunder...
Baowuga removed her eyepatch. Her right eye began to blaze with dazzling light.
This was the priestesses' trump card, passed down through generations and used only when all else was lost.
Using it deliberately consumed an enormous amount of life force, and the slightest misstep could end that life.
Put the other way: if one had truly resolved, one could unleash tremendous power at the cost of one's life.
The power gathered at her eye, her vision began to blur, and she seemed to see an illusion—
She saw two people who should not have been there standing before her.
They should not have been here.
That's enough, Baowuga.
Orchid took Baowuga's hand and gently drew her out of the dense fog.
And Catapult, as a matter of course, put her behind her.
You should not have come. Now all my effort is undone!
That hurts...
The Lord of Thunder rose slowly, its towering frame casting a shadow over them all.
Yet neither Orchid nor Catapult gave any sign of retreating.
...Why?
There really is a child at our side who looks exactly like you.
...You look alike, but your temperaments are complete opposites.
I think of her — Popukar — as a little sister. She's timid and short on will, and if no one pulled her forward she'd stay in one spot alone until the world ended.
But I'm only her squad leader while she's at Rhodes Island. I can't be her leader all her life.
She has to learn to stand on her own.
I don't mean to demand that she become any particular kind of person... but she should at least learn to think about what kind of person she wants to be.
And you — you're independent, you act, you know what you want.
I did have the thought once: it would be good if Popukar were a little more like you.
But I let go of that quickly. Because Baowuga is Baowuga and Popukar is Popukar.
Right now, at least, I'd like you to be a little more like her — to learn to lean on other people.
You two...
Next time you walk off like that on your own, I'll rap your head considerably harder.
I... was not wrong.
Even if you had not come, I could have fulfilled my mission.
There's no such thing as a mission written in stone.
(A wary growl)
Orchid, Catapult, get Her Majesty out of here first, meow!
Why, meow?!
Look at the Lord of Thunder—
(A roar of utter fury)
Is it helping us?
The black miasma coming off it has thinned a great deal... Perhaps the fight with Baowuga brought it round.
Right. If it really isn't some evil thing, and it carries the previous sovereign's power, then it makes sense it would see these curse-fiends as the real threat.
Or perhaps the Zinogre simply judges the curse-fiends to be more of a threat than you, meow!
I'm not that naive. But we all heard the previous sovereign's last words.
She said not to fight the Lord of Thunder, but to use its power.
...What?!
How could that be?! What reason would my mother have...
And besides, even so, the Lord of Thunder hurt Midnight and raised the beast tide!
That sound is—
Samurai? Why are you — could it be—
Your Majesty.
Midnight, are you all right?!
Hmph. Does he look all right to you?
He insisted I haul him here on my machine.
Your Majesty, I have a thousand things to tell you. But one of them is surely the most urgent.
The Lord of Thunder may not be the culprit.
You mean the Lord of Thunder saved you?!
Just so.
At the time I was caught in the blast with curse-fiends closing in, and I thought I was certain to die. It was then the Lord of Thunder appeared and swept them away.
What happened after that, I do not know.
Wait — so what I saw wasn't the Lord of Thunder striking you down with curse-fiends. It saved you, and then stood there purifying those curse-fiends with the priestess's power?!
I am afraid... that is so.
When I woke and learned where Her Majesty had gone, I set out at once to tell you this.
So my mother truly entrusted her power to the Lord of Thunder?
...And yet that is not impossible to explain.
If the Lord of Thunder was never the spreader of the curse but a victim of it...
If my mother knew that it had been devouring curse-infected beasts by instinct all along...
And if the reason it has survived despite absorbing the curse is that my mother gave it her power...

Then the Lord of Thunder we saw in the past was not the cause of disaster. It appeared there because it was drawn to disaster...
The true culprit...
is the curse — or rather, the Wheel?!
So the Lord of Thunder isn't our enemy, at least?
(A wary growl)
That's right... The curse-fiends also seem to be closing on the Wheel, meow.
I don't know what they intend, but it is certainly nothing good, meow...
Whatever the case, my power alone is not enough to fully activate the Wheel. I need the part of my mother's power that resides in the Lord of Thunder.
Then can't we get it to help us?
Help?
It is only a beast—
Beasts have instincts too. They at least know what threatens them most, or it wouldn't be picking off curse-fiends. Right?
...Fair point.
Even if it can't understand us, so long as it knows what the greatest threat is, it's our ally by default.
Which means the objective is set. Right, Captain?
Captain?
That's right.
Orchid noticed that Baowuga and Midnight were nodding too.
One of you is a Shogun and the other a sovereign. Why are you looking at me?
I... still believe my way was not wrong. But I must admit your way may be better.
Right now, you can make a sounder judgment than I can.
Had Miss Orchid not commanded the army in my place after I fell, Mirage would already be in chaos. The letter you left gave me courage as well. The hunting corps is yours to command.
If not for Catapult's weapon, I couldn't have developed Banmira's custom Dragonator. Point, and I'll fire!
Er... so that thing actually worked! I thought you were just having us on!
Of course it works! How many times must I say it — I'm a proper inventor!
Then at least fix your taste in names!
Give the order, Orchid.
What am I to do with you lot.
Very well. I'll assign the combat tasks.
Beasts ringed them on every side; the situation was dire.
Orchid felt her mind clearer than it had ever been.
The objective is to reach the Lord of Thunder.
But our purpose isn't to hunt it — it's to help it break free of the curse entirely.
Midnight, you and your men take the vanguard and open the way.
Understood. I will not fail you.
Banmira, you support Midnight.
Support him how?
Blow things up to your heart's content, however you like.
Ha! Now that I like!
Catapult, you and I cover Baowuga.
Got it!
Baowuga.
I am here.
Your task is—
to leave nothing you'll regret.
...Understood.
This mission is extremely dangerous. Don't push beyond what you can do.
And when we succeed... I'll treat you all to grilled meat.
That's so stingy, Orchid!
If you're unhappy, go find another captain.
I'd rather not, heh heh.
It feels like it's been a while since we were all together like this.
This really is how A6 ought to be.
Why do I feel like Yoshitsune and I are being left out, meow?!
(An indignant snort)
I want grilled meat too, meow!
All right, all right. You can do the grilling. Satisfied?
Now that's more like it, meow!
Let's move out.
All of you, listen!
I have made a grave mistake.
I have spoken constantly of the nation's survival, of the meaning of the trial, of the Lord of Thunder's strength. But in the end, I believe I was afraid to face it.
Once fear takes hold of a thing, a person shrinks back and finds all manner of excuses to flee from it.
Founding the hunting corps, training you as soldiers, stopping Her Majesty from challenging the Lord of Thunder — none of that came from far-sighted wisdom. It came only from this:
I was not strong enough.
I even passed that fear on to you.
I demanded prudence of you, demanded that you learn to act as circumstances allowed, demanded that you not stake your lives on a hunt...
But I failed to pass on the most important thing of all.
Haah. You're always so pessimistic and so arrogant at once.
Even if Mirage really were destroyed, it wouldn't be your responsibility alone.
Just so, Shogun. As you have always taught us, we did not choose caution out of blind obedience to your orders.
We chose to join the hunting corps, we chose to guard our home as samurai, because we too believed it was right!
You have never done anything wrong. If we truly fail, it is only that we were not good enough. Nothing more.
You are right. Perhaps instead of regret I should feel fortunate.
Fortunate to have learned the truth at last; fortunate not to have become the unfeeling man I imagined.
Fortunate that even now there is still something I can do for Her Majesty.
Your Majesty.
I kept convincing myself that I was not wrong, kept telling myself that among many poor options I had chosen the relatively right one.
In time it somehow became the only answer...
I should have talked with you far more. I should have worked alongside you long ago.
In that, perhaps I was the same.
When we return, I shall speak with you openly.

I look forward to that day.
Hunting corps, to order!
Sir!
Advance by formation and open the way for Her Majesty Baowuga and the monster hunters!
For our future!
Yes, sir!
Charge! For Mirage, for Her Majesty Baowuga!
Ha ha, let me lend a hand as well!
Honestly, old friend.
The world really is impossible to predict.
Never once managing the things you set out to do — and then, just when you're sure you're about to fail, you suddenly find you haven't failed quite so badly after all.
You wouldn't understand. In the world of invention, that sort of thing happens roughly once a day!
Success is always accidental! But so long as the result is good enough, what's the harm?
Ha. You're right about that.
Your Majesty, go!
Your Majesty, call for me if you need fire support. It'll give me a chance to test the range!
I shall!
This place... this altar... The people of old Mirage stood here...
The closer I come, the more clearly I feel the curse.
At last I understand what that force pulling at me on the snowy mountain truly was...
I thought it was the Lord of Thunder, but it must have been the Wheel. All along, it was the Wheel drawing at me...
Mother — the source of everything, the truth of the trial, is the Wheel. Is that so?
I have come, Lord of Thunder.
Baowuga, now!
Yes!
I beg you, Lord of Thunder. We ask only that you lend us your power!
Ngh—
What do we do, Orchid? It doesn't seem to be working!
Tch. A stubborn creature.
We've dealt it so much damage and it shows no fear at all. If anything, it grows fiercer as it fights.
Has the curse robbed it of its will?
Or is it—
Orchid, something's wrong. Look at the Lord of Thunder—
The change came abruptly.
Having broken free of Baowuga's power, this time the Lord of Thunder did not lunge. Instead it began to howl in agony.
Its body thrashed ceaselessly, black miasma rising off it like steam — a sight to chill the blood.
Orchid, look at it! It looks like the curse is about to devour it completely! Do we have no choice but to kill it?
...Catapult, we can't hold back anymore.
If the Lord of Thunder truly is devoured by the curse, it will bring catastrophe.
...Understood.
Baowuga, do you understand?
Don't think about anything else. We've done everything we could. Whatever the outcome, all we can do is accept it.
...Yes.

Now, while it's still struggling, let's—
Huh?
Thunderbugs?
When did they...
They're flying in from the bamboo grove!
At some point, a blue-green "bridge" had risen through the dim underground ruins.
And what formed that bridge were the Thunderbugs coming from the direction of the underground grove.
More and more of them began circling the Lord of Thunder, as if gathering toward something.
As the Thunderbugs multiplied, the black miasma on the Lord of Thunder grew thicker as well.
And yet, lit by that blue-green glow, the Lord of Thunder seemed less befouled, and carried a trace more of dangerous beauty.
Were they summoned by the Lord of Thunder? But... why?
Lord of Thunder, could you—
Orchid, I've got a feeling.
It isn't fully tainted by the curse... it's been fighting the curse all this time. And right now, it's about to win?
While everyone hesitated, the Lord of Thunder's agony seemed to ease, and it sprang nimbly to a higher ledge.
It stood there, raised its head high, and let out a long, drawn-out roar.
And then — the earth split and the mountain came down.
Ngh— I can still fight!
Don't push yourself. Another samurai has taken your post. Rest properly now!
I— I killed several beasts! I didn't shame the Shogun!
Rest easy. Everyone did well. Now get some rest.
(Quietly) Your Majesty, Master Banmira, all of you — we'll keep our nation safe, so please, please come back unharmed...
Huh...
Hm?
Are my eyes playing tricks? Why does it look like storm clouds are gathering over the Wheel?
Throughout Mirage City, people raised their heads together and looked toward the Wheel—
A thick bolt of lightning tore through the night's clouds and struck the snowy mountain toward the Wheel.
Anyone standing closer would have seen that the bolt had punched a great hole in the ground, and that what lay beyond it was bottomless.
But they would certainly have heard the earth-shaking roar that came up from below—
It was a roar full of wildness.
With that roar, the thick bolt pierced rock that had perhaps never been so solid to begin with, and struck the Lord of Thunder.
It was only an instant of lightning, and yet the whole dim underground seemed to shudder with it.
Bathed in that light, the Lord of Thunder seemed to complete one last transformation, and roared again.
This time, blue-green lightning wound about its entire body.
Its bristling mane was like white surf frozen mid-crash, every strand wrapped in lightning, arcs bursting at the tips and scattering broken stars.
Its scales were like jade, with rivers of gold and white running between them. When its tail swept, sparks drew amber whips through the air, tearing rents in the darkness.
Through the hole the lightning had opened, a thread of moonlight spilled down.
Under that moonlight, it seemed the most noble king in all the world.
Every beast stopped moving in that moment.
Did it... clear the curse itself, using the lightning?
No, Orchid, look closely.
The curse's black miasma is still coming off it... but the way it moves looks completely different from before...
It didn't clear the curse — it overcame it, and turned the curse entirely into part of its own strength!
Orchid, it seems we were making work for ourselves.
...Indeed. Nothing on this earth can ever be taken as a rule.
We thought we'd gained the crucial information from the previous sovereign, and that our task was to save the Lord of Thunder.
We set our hearts on saving it, on freeing it from the abyss of the curse...
And in the end, it doesn't seem to have needed saving.
Not necessarily.
Beasts always hone themselves in battle. Without fighting us, it might not have overcome the curse at all.
Seen that way, we did "save" it, didn't we?
...Perhaps.
Your Majesty, now — use Wyvern Riding on it, meow!
Make its power yours, meow!
I shall try—
A bolt lashed down and struck the Wirebug from Baowuga's hand. The Lord of Thunder snorted disdainfully, plainly displeased.
But it took no further action, and simply watched her quietly.
As though waiting for something.
It seems that unless you defeat it outright, it won't let you ride it.
...Indeed.
Since learning the truth, I have felt guilt toward you, Lord of Thunder.
After all, you were only a victim of the curse — and had you not preyed on cursed beasts by instinct, the curse might have spread faster still.
But it was not we who brought you to Mirage, and for all these years my nation and my people have lived beneath your shadow.
And whatever else is true, my most beloved mother died by your hand...
I cannot set aside my resentment so lightly either.
(A low growl)
It doesn't understand a word of that, Baowuga.
It's a beast. It doesn't agonize over its lot because the Wheel dropped it into a strange land, nor curse its fate because the curse afflicted it.
It simply shoulders all of it according to its nature.
Brought to a new world, it lives in the new world.
Afflicted by the curse, it overcomes the curse.
Curse-fiends try to kill it, so it kills them.
Beyond that, it doesn't care whether you hate it or love it. To it, that isn't important...
Life's instinct is simply to live.
Right. Even with the Wheel looming as a threat, it still won't join hands with us.
After all, what we're trying to do challenges its dignity as a king.
In the end, it comes down to the weapons in our hands.
...That is true.
The sun rose. It was a fine day for a hunt.
Yoshitsune, stand back!
(An indignant growl)
All right, then there's no problem going in together, is there?
(A roar full of fighting spirit)
Hah, I've seen right through this move already, Lord of Thunder!
Yoshitsune!
Hah, I won't let you have it that easily!
(An enraged roar)
You're strong, Lord of Thunder. If you weren't this strong, I'd never have wanted to get stronger myself.
I know this isn't all you've got, is it?
Come on, Lord of Thunder. I've caught up. Show me more of what you can be.
(A warning growl)
Heh heh, that move again? Bring it on!
How was that, Yoshitsune?!
(A grudgingly approving snort)

You're no fun at all!
Still...
Orchid!
What is it?
Don't you always say that if you never try, you'll never find what suits you?
And?
I always used to wonder why you believed life had some kind of answer in it. I never thought so.
What, has something dawned on you today?
I don't know.

lines.st: Is it now?
Is it this moment?
Catapult didn't know.
She only knew that something hot was surging through her body.
She must be smiling right now. Smiling very happily.

lines.x: Shogun, aren't you joining the hunt?
...No. The man I am now has no right to.
This hunt belongs to Her Majesty and the monster hunters.
But... as I said before, I made a mistake, and now is the best chance I have to make up for it.
I want you to witness this hunt with me, and to carve it into your hearts.
Then take what you have seen and heard back to our capital, and pass it down.
These ten years, in our struggle to survive, we all but forgot what hunting means... It is time we took it up again.
Yes, sir!
Orchid, it's coming your way!
I know!
That girl Catapult... she's thoroughly enjoying herself.
Catapult has completely adapted to the Zinogre's offense, meow... Her handling of every move is textbook, meow...
Orchid, we cannot fall behind, meow!
Why exactly must I compete with her?
A hunter hones their craft and climbs to greater heights, meow!
And when, may I ask, did I become a hunter?
Still...
Letting go like this once in a while isn't bad.
She felt the wind of the Lord of Thunder's claws passing her ear, and somehow the corners of her mouth lifted a little.
Nock. Loose.
And then a howl of pain rang out. She had long since spotted its weak point — and, to her own mild surprise, she had somehow grown used to the bow in her hands.
I don't know why, but seeing Orchid smile suddenly sends a chill down my back...
Oi, if you need help, just say the word.
Banmira's custom Dragonator can fire at any time!
Tch. The lot of them are hooked and can't hear a word I say. Doesn't look like I'm needed.
Baowuga, here it comes! Get behind me!
Understood!
Now!
Haaah—!
Hah— hah—
It worked, meow! The Zinogre's body no longer rejects the Wirebug, meow!
Now, Your Majesty, meow!
Ride it, Baowuga! Leave the rest to us!
Go, Baowuga!
Go and end all of this!
Understood!
Under Baowuga's control, the Lord of Thunder leapt high and landed upon a raised platform.
Then Baowuga's body began to give off a deep blue light — like a bright moon in that still-dark underground.
And the Lord of Thunder howled at the sky. Storm clouds gathered above, as if a thunderstorm were about to break.
In the next instant, the beam from Baowuga's eye and the lightning the Lord of Thunder called down crossed together at the center of the Wheel.
And then came a sight none of them would ever forget—
The beam and the lightning were wholly absorbed, and at the Wheel's center a tiny point appeared.
No — "appeared" is not quite right. The point was more like a hole torn in the space there. It spread gradually until it filled the entire Wheel—
And then, with the Wheel at its center, a colorless wave burst violently outward.
Everywhere it reached, the cursed beasts fell one after another, and the marks the curse had left on them faded away.
The curse is all gone, meow!
(A joyful roar)
Your Majesty! You did it!
Ha! So that's how the Wheel is meant to be used! It seems we never truly understood this great thing at all!
So it's finally over!
Wait — what's that? Inside the Wheel—
Before Orchid could finish, a prism of light shot out of the open void, struck directly below the Wheel, and engulfed them all.
Where is this...?
I seem... to have been struck by a beam of light... and I can feel that it is very like the power within me...

lines.st: Well done.

lines.x: This voice... Mother?!

lines.st: Baowuga, my daughter, you have done it.

lines.x: Mother, is it truly you?!

lines.st: I am sorry, Baowuga. Had I been able to return to your side, you would not have had to carry so much.

lines.x: What happened, Mother?
What made you choose, in the end, to give your power to the Lord of Thunder?

lines.st: While hunting the Lord of Thunder I came to these ruins of our ancestors, and here I found the truth about the Wheel—
Our forebears came to this land through the Wheel and founded Mirage, and our line were the Wheel's operators.
But as time passed, the Wheel lost the great part of its power and began leaking the curse outward, until at last it brought catastrophe.

lines.x: That is... the disaster recorded in the histories that nearly destroyed Mirage...

lines.st: It was two of our forebears who halted that disaster...
At the cost of their own lives they activated the Wheel fully, and only then was the curse wholly dispelled.
The disaster came too suddenly. Only one priestess, still a child, was escorted to safety — and worse, Mirage lost far too much of its history and inheritance.
Not even the truth of that history could be left to us.
This is only my conjecture — our two forebears never repaired the Wheel. They merely halted the leaking of the curse with their own power.
Which is to say, they made the Wheel what it is today.

lines.x: You mean... the Wheel is the source of everything, and the so-called trial is merely an accident born of its damage?!
That we presumed to treat the monster as our enemy and the monster hunters as our allies? If... if that is so, then what of Mirage's inheritance...

lines.st: And what of it, Baowuga, my beloved daughter?
The strong devour the weak. Such is the way of nature.
Whether this is a trial or an accident, we have made hunting our foundation and carried our line to this day. Who can say we were wrong?
Only, at the same time as I found these ruins, I realized the Wheel's next eruption was no longer far off.
But by then the curse had eaten deep into me as well, and I could scarcely hold on to a clear mind. That was why I made that decision.

lines.x: So you chose to give your power to the Lord of Thunder, and waited for me or some descendant to discover the secret it carried.
The Lord of Thunder is strong enough to absorb far more of the curse, and so can wield a greater priestess's power...
Which means that if I could fully absorb the priestess's power within it, I too could pay with my life and fully activate the Wheel.

lines.st: You insist that is the only right way, do you not?

lines.x: I... of course do not believe that.
But it is my mission.

lines.st: I passed on to you the responsibility of a sovereign and the mission of a priestess, yet never taught you how to carry those burdens together with others.
I entrusted the duty of supporting you to Midnight, yet never taught him how to walk alongside you.
That is my responsibility.
...No. Perhaps even had I lived, I could not have managed it.
You are so very like me, Baowuga.

lines.x: Huh...?
Baowuga noticed a Thunderbug alight on her shoulder, and then her body began to move of its own accord.
(Mother is moving my body?!)
In the final moment of my life, I made the decision to give my power to the Lord of Thunder.
A priestess's power cannot be handed over lightly; it is possible only by seizing the instant between life and death.
And so I went before the Lord of Thunder of my own will.
We, the people of Mirage, carry out heaven's decree and hunt the beasts of the earth.
When I stood before it with what reason remained to me, I thought my heart would be at peace.
To stake one's life killing the prey is to honor it, and to die at the prey's hand is a hunter's proper death.
And yet I was wrong.
"Baowuga" took her stance, charged the Lord of Thunder, and swung with all her strength.
The next instant, dense mist rose, and everything vanished like a bubble.

lines.st: In that last moment, what filled my mind was this—
Had I trusted Masamune and Yoshitsune a little more, had I shared a little more of the burden with Midnight, perhaps it need never have come to this.

lines.x: Baowuga?!
How are you—
Miss Catapult, Miss Orchid?! Where is this...
Where's the Lord of Thunder?
I can no longer feel its presence.
Perhaps it has already returned to its own home.
But I have a feeling — this may be our road home.
Now that you say it, this does look familiar. Isn't this the bamboo grove we came through when we arrived in Mirage?!
...It is. It seems it's time to go home.
Huh? Could it be—
Ha, that's right, I can hear the sandstorm!
Time to go back, Orchid!
It seems our mission really is over.
Wait, I... I have not yet said a proper farewell!
Partings are always sudden, Baowuga.
Back home there's a child just like you who needs help, waiting for us.
My willfulness caused you a great deal of trouble. Thank you.
Don't say that. I've had a wonderful time!
...Indeed.
If this was a dream, then it was the loveliest dream I've had in a long while.
Orchid, the sandstorm's getting quieter. We have to hurry!
Right.
Baowuga, remember this.
You're strong and you know your own mind. There really are many things you can handle yourself.
But—
Living is the process of discovering you aren't all-powerful.
When the day comes that you realize that again, learn to ask the people beside you for help. Understood?
Otherwise, even with a whole Wheel between us, I'll come and rap you on the head.
...All right.
Lecturing to the very end. That's Orchid for you!
This is who I am. Don't like it?
Heh heh, I love it!
Let's go. We're running out of time.
Wait, what about us, meow?!
Oh right, I nearly forgot you two!
Your mission is over too, isn't it?
The Lord of Thunder's threat is gone, and it seems the so-called curse was not the Frenzy Virus after all — the Frenzy Virus could never do such a thing, meow!
Yoshitsune's mission and mine are indeed over, but there seems to be no road back to Kamura Village from here, meow!
Baowuga, can you open the Wheel again?
No. I can feel it — the Wheel has lost its power entirely. To activate it again would take a very long time.
How long, meow?
I do not know... And I now know that activating it rashly invites ill results.
Then what do we do, meow?!
Er, why don't you two come with us for now!
Maybe Kamura Village is in Higashi!
Hm. In any case, as members of the Hidden Team, exploring the unknown is part of our duty, meow!
We might even bring back some unheard-of local specialties for our friends in Kamura, meow!
(An approving roar)
Then it's settled!
Your Majesty, farewell, meow!
(A parting roar)
Bye, Baowuga! Be happy!
Don't push yourself too hard.
Farewell.
I shall remember you always.

eps.name: The Dream Ends, the Hunting Spirit Does Not

lines.x: The wind was the only master of this chaos.
With his enormous shield, Spot was struggling to hold a small, precarious pocket of safety for himself and for Popukar behind him.
Cough, cough... What a pain! This sand is getting into my lungs! Midnight, how's it going over there?!
Well enough! I've dealt with the last two sand bandits! And you? Is Popukar all right?
She's perfectly fine, tucked behind me the whole time, hasn't eaten a single grain! It's you — if you're done, hurry up and help! I can't hold much longer!
My new manga is waiting for me back at Rhodes Island. I'm not dying out here for nothing!
Calm down, Spot. Hold on a little longer. Miss Orchid and Catapult will come to back us up!
(This is terrifying... The sand's so thick... I can't see anything...)
(Spot... his shield is shaking... he can't hold much longer...)
(Huh? That person... a sand bandit! He got past Midnight!)
Spot!
Spot, behind you!
What?!
(He can't turn in time! That blade... that blade is coming down!)
(No— don't hurt Spot!)
Something strange and searing welled up from behind her eyes.
She had no time even to wonder what it was, and on pure instinct she turned that force toward the bandit.
A beam of energy, almost invisible, flashed from her eyes.
It hit no one.
Hmmm—
A strange hum, as though from beyond the world, rang out, and an unseen shockwave spread from it.
What was that just now?!
No idea! Something blew up? Hey! Popukar, are you all right?!
Mm... Popukar's fine...
Popukar stood blankly where she was. She didn't know what had just happened either. She only saw that the bad man had gone flying and Spot was safe.
...Is it over?
Are we... back?
I think so... That hunt just now... the Wheel... Baowuga... How much time has passed?
A clear cry, utterly out of place in this desert, sounded behind them.
Is this place... the distant sealed land, meow?
(A disappointed whine)
Masamune?! Yoshitsune?!
So it wasn't a dream after all.
Miss Orchid! Catapult! Where did you two go?!
Hey—! You two dropped out of contact for over a minute. I thought you'd been buried in the sand!
Orchid and Catapult turned to see their own familiar Midnight, Spot and Popukar running toward them.

A strange wind came up out of nowhere and then we lost contact. We were beside ourselves! At least the fighting's over.
Are you both all right?
Huh, when did you change clothes? Rather distinctive.
Never mind the clothes — where did the cloud beast and the fanged beast behind you come from? They look well fed.
Orchid! Catapult! I'm so glad you're both all right!
Looking at these three all-too-familiar "problem children" before her, and then at the two new companions behind her, Orchid didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
For a moment she thought of the self-possessed Baowuga, of that cheerful Banmira, of the Midnight who had grown so stubborn in protecting the people and the nation he loved.
She felt she had changed — grown a little gentler.
I'll tell you the details in time.
In short: Midnight, Spot, Popukar — I'm glad you're all safe. The mess of this mission was my failure of command. I worried you, and you did well.
Hm? What is it?
Hey, hey, who are you? You're not our captain. Our captain just sighs and calls us problem children.
Indeed... That gentle tone, that frank apology... Miss, were you possessed by something in that sandstorm?
I know a few ladies well versed in the occult. Shall we go and have you looked at?
Uh-oh.

...
You two! I try to be a decent captain for once and you don't like it?! Mission reports!
Now!
Immediately!
This instant!
Write down everything that happened, in full detail! And Midnight — where exactly did you meet these ladies well versed in the occult, hm?
Reporting, Captain: that is a long story!
Ah... This time it really is Orchid. I'll get back to my manga, then. Midnight, once you work out what happened, let me know.
Thirty words or fewer, preferably.
Mm, sometimes I do think certain things really aren't Orchid's fault.
Orchid!
Haah. Our Popukar really is the best of you.
Oh, Masamune.
Meow?
How about this: why don't you two come back with us first?
Your home, meow?
That's right. A fine place called Rhodes Island.
The market in the west quarter could be expanded further. Banmira, it is time the people saw those new inventions of yours as well.
No problem, Your Majesty! My latest improved "fully automatic Bunny Dango maker" will let everyone enjoy delicious dango any time, anywhere!
Before that, I believe there is one more thing to do. We should raise a statue to our heroes in the capital's central square.
Yes... For Miss Orchid and Miss Catapult, for Lord Masamune and Lord Yoshitsune, and for all the monster hunters who came before.
May they have returned safely to their homes.
And if it can be done, I would like a statue for the Lord of Thunder as well.
Why is that?
Not to honor it, nor to pity it... only to remember it.
...Very well.
Mirage ought indeed to remember the Lord of Thunder.
What we can do is pass down their story, together with this nation's history, forever.
Come to think of it, I do miss them a little. Catapult was always laughing at my inventions, but without her weapon I could never have built the Dragonator.
And Masamune — that one never stops talking, but everything he gave us was the genuine article...
Yes... Somehow, though everything is peaceful now, it feels... a little empty.
Midnight's eyes met Baowuga's again, and this time there was no wall between them, and no opposition.
Just then, a samurai came in wearing a curious expression.
Reporting to Your Majesty and the Shogun... Two hunters outside the city request an audience.
Hunters? From where?
They say... they come from a distant land—
Baowuga's heart stirred with an indescribable premonition. She strode out of the council hall and came to the city gate.
Outside the gate stood two travel-worn figures.
One wore an elegant hunter's set like violet flame and carried a longbow, scanning the surroundings warily.
The other wore blue-green armor and had a wild air about her, an enormous sword and shield strapped to her back, idly kicking a pebble with her toe.
Their clothing, their bearing, their weapons... all differed somewhat from the two in Baowuga's memory.
But those two faces were exactly the same.
I heard there were beasts here worth challenging, which is why I came all this way. Don't tell me you mean to take them from me?
I only heard that the beasts around Mirage carry very rare materials. If the rumor is true, then may the better hunter win.
Ha, suits me fine!
...Miss Orchid?
...Miss Catapult?
The tearing of space and time lasted only an instant.
When the Zinogre opened its eyes again, what met it was no longer the dead, dust-and-curse-laden air of Mirage's underground ruins.
It was wind.
Wind carrying damp earth, the scent of grass, and cool mist. The wind it had known intimately since the day it was born.

It raised its head. Clear moonlight passed through the dense canopy and scattered dappled silver over the mossy ground. It heard a waterfall roaring in the distance, and insects calling among the trees.
It had come home.
The heavy priestess's power that had been pressed inside it for ten years was gone, and the foul curse tangled in its soul had dissolved like smoke.
It let out a long roar, no longer carrying pain or rage. That roar was not to threaten but to declare: the true king of these mountains had returned.
It began to run.
Powerful limbs leapt through the trees, sharp claws tore up familiar soil, its strong body shouldered aside the brush in its path.
It bounded over a rushing stream and paused beneath a waterfall, letting the cold spray wash over its scarred scales and rinse away dust that did not belong to this world.
Following memory, it found a cliff. That was its throne. It lay down quietly, pillowed its great head on its forepaws, and coiled its long golden tail beside it like a weary snake.
It closed its eyes and sank peacefully into sleep.
Snap.
A faint breaking twig made its ear twitch sharply.
Its eyes opened at once, beast-pupils bright in the dark, all sleep gone.
It had heard it.
A steady, rhythmic footfall belonging to a two-legged creature. One step, then another, approaching neither hurried nor slow.
In those steps there was no fear. Only resolve.
The Zinogre rose slowly and looked toward the sound. A figure stepped out of the shadows of the trees.
It was a hunter, wearing a broad bamboo hat and a red-and-blue cloud-knot garb, wooden clogs striking the rock with a light, crisp clack.
In his hand was a slender long sword, its blade reflecting a contained, keen light in the moonlight.
He too saw the Zinogre on the cliff.
Their eyes met.
There was no hatred. No fear.
The Zinogre's muscles began to swell, threads of golden lightning leaping and flickering across its jade-blue scales. It lowered its head and gave a low roar brimming with the will to fight.
This was an ancient fate, written into its blood.
It did not understand what a "hero" was, nor did it care what "sacrifice" meant.
It knew only that in its world, when one strong thing met another, battle was the only — and the highest — form of respect.
